definitions.volume_index: weekly hard RESISTANCE sets (or sets per exercise when the slot count is constant) / week 1 x 100. Athletic work (plyo contacts, throws, sprints, Olympic lifts) is tracked separately.
definitions.total_index: athlete skeletons only: all working sets incl. athletic (excluding med-ball throws and conditioning) / week 1 x 100
definitions.set_counting: v1: 1 hard set = 1.0 to the main mover + 0.25 to each helper (COACH-ANSWER VOL-09); dips 0.5 triceps + 0.5 chest (LIB-16); a 10/10 unilateral set = 1 set (UNI-01). Athletic sets (plyo, ballistic, throws, Olympic, sprints) never count toward muscles (VOL-10). Pelland 0.5 is kept only as a research comparison (12_volume_algorithm_v1). v1.1: KB swings are ballistic/athletic and never count as glute volume; compounds (squats, lunges, deadlifts, RDLs) credit glutes 0.25; a thruster = 1.0 quads, 0.5 shoulders, 0.25 glutes (COACH-R2 R2-VOL-05). v1.2: counting on focus groups: hips = glutes + hamstrings (e.g. RDL + hip thrust + leg curl = 3 hip exercises), shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor; users and coaches can add more rear-delt work); 2-4 exercises per group trained that day; calves one exercise x 3 sets per leg day; Focus muscle 1 / 2 (optional, max 2) get +1 to +3 weekly sets each inside the stairway (COACH-R3 R3-SES-01, R3-VOL-01).
definitions.ref_sets: weekly hard sets of one reference BIG muscle (start L1 10 / L2 15 / L3 20; cap 14 / 22 / 25) moved by the v1.1 stairway (target T(w) = T(w-1) x (1 + λ step), whole sets placed while T - current >= 1); computed by p06v11/curves.py with the method of 12_volume_algorithm v1.1 §3.7.1-3.8; v1.2: the same curves, steps approved in COACH-R3 R3-VOL-04 (12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.7.1-3.8)
definitions.training_block_v1_1: one stairway plan unit (a 12- or 8-week block, a year block, a week-by-week stairway); what R2-VOL-07 calls 'a block': completed or cancelled as a whole
definitions.exercise_block_v1_1: the 4-6-week stretch inside a training block where the exercises stay fixed (PER-02); 12-week = 1-4 / 5-8 / 9-12, 8-week = 1-4 / 5-8
definitions.stair_level_v1_1: display number 2..11 for how hard a week should feel (R2-PER-05): week 1 = 2, last week = 11 (PROPOSED display)
definitions.planned_step_pct_v1_1: the stairway step into a week when there is no check-in (R2-VOL-03): 3 % to the halfway week, then 5 %, multiplied by one factor λ per muscle so its planned peak lands on its cap in the last week; older adults <= 3 % (PROPOSED; same method as 12_volume_algorithm v1.1 §3.7.1)
definitions.training_block_v1_2: one stairway plan unit (a 12- or 8-week block, a year block), printed whole; completed or stopped as a whole (R2-VOL-07); when it ends the user builds the next (R3-PER-01)
definitions.planned_step_pct_v1_2: the approved stairway step into a week (R3-VOL-04): about 3 % to the halfway week, then about 5 %, multiplied by one factor λ per group so its planned peak lands on its cap in the last week; the only step - there are no check-ins (R3-VOL-02); older adults: the same steps (the v1.1 PROPOSED <= 3 % cap is retired, 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.4)
definitions.rate_cap_pct: RETIRED in v1.2 (it was the most a check-in could give); removed from the skeleton rows and grids

verification_log: CrossFit macro (2.2, OBS_CF_MACRO): the claim that 'each block restarts aerobic and WOD levels higher' was WRONG. Aerobic runs 1-2-3 | 1-2-3-4 | 2-3-4 and WODs 2-3 | 2-3-4 | 2-3-4, so only block 3 restarts aerobic higher. 'Resistance rides with strength' is false for block 1 (FEB-MARCH resistance alone, APRIL strength + power). Added: the AUGUST grid marks 2 WOD days at WOD level 3.

CrossFit FULL TIME '+5.5 %/week' (rule 4, table 2.3) was presented as an observed rate. The macro never walks strength L1-L2-L3-L4 in consecutive months (L1 APRIL, L3 JUNE, L4 JULY, L2 OCT/NOV), so the rate is relabelled INFERRED (a hypothetical walk of the dose table).

Effort grammar (rule 6/R6, 5.1, strength rules) was presented as OBSERVED 'nuance = unilateral MAX, survival = isolation ALL'. It is a splice of STRENGTH-12 slot names with STRENGTH-8 effort words. In STRENGTH-8 and the CONJUGATE draft the 'MAX' rows are pull-ups / DB rows, alt incline DB bench and lunges, and the 'ALL' rows are RFE lunges / staggered DL and bicep curls. The class mapping is now marked INFERRED.

Dynamic-effort effort: STRENGTH-8 and the CONJUGATE draft label the fast rows '1RIR' (4T D18/D21). The STRENGTH_8 skeleton had borrowed STRENGTH-12's 'FAST RPE6 or about 60-70%' as if it were STRENGTH-8's own label. Fixed, flagged as a conflict, and added as an open question.

STRENGTH_8 week-1 doses were wrong. DE sets are 5 on Thursday but 3 on Saturday (B18/B21). Accessory sets are 3-4, not 3. The 'ALL' rows are 2-3 x '8/8' (not '8/8' or 10). The 10-rep rows are the 'MAX' rows. Added: the green ladder fill also covers B17 (plyo) and B21. The week-8 weekly set count of 10 is now marked INFERRED, and the 'the work' label for the plyo row is attributed to the CONJUGATE draft (M21).

STRENGTH_12 week 1: 'TATE PRESS' 3x20 was attributed to 'the survival'. It sits in the Wednesday NUANCE slot (N15). Also: main-lift reps per session are 18-20 in weeks 1-10 but 14 in weeks 11-12, not 'held 18-20'. The STRENGTH-12 'A/B weeks' are an analyst label: there are no 'A WEEK'/'B WEEK' cells.

Its rows were marked OBSERVED with '1-2 RIR' / '1 RIR' / '0-1 RIR' efforts borrowed from AESTHETICS-8 col D, so effort is now marked INFERRED. Also flagged: in weeks 4-6 the SETS row says 4 while the rep string lists 3 numbers before '-20'. Reading '-20' as the isolation reps is INFERRED.
AESTHETICS-12 week-12 overreach: chest (32.5 sets) was omitted from the '33-35 sets' list.

Science - plyometric volume: 'newer recommendations allow up to ~200 high-intensity or ~400 low-intensity contacts/session' is NOT supported by the cited PMC7873906 table, which is a study protocol of 72 -> 126 contacts/session. Removed.

Science - RP landmarks: the cited arvo.guru page gives no per-muscle numbers, and the quoted ranges did not match RP's own guides (e.g. biceps was 4-6/10-14/14-20; RP gives MEV 8-10, MAV 14-20, MRV 20-26). Replaced with RP's published chest/quads/biceps/triceps/calves values; back is marked not extracted. The governor cross-check was updated to match.

Science - Bell 2022 (Front Sports Act Living) is a qualitative interview study of 18 coaches, not a survey (deloads ~every 4-6 weeks, ~1 week). Westside dynamic effort is ~50-60 % bar weight plus band/chain tension, not '60-70 %'. Plotkin 2022 used lower-body exercises, so it does not support a small-muscle-only rule. All three have caveats.

corrections: Effort grammar (rule 6, R6, L04, table 5.1, strength rules): the 'MAX' on Thursday's lunges (D20) was filed under the 3rd row 'the nuance'. On Thursday the plyo row takes 'the work' position, so the DE squat is 'the accessory' ('1RIR'), pull-ups are 'the nuance' at '2RIR' (D19, M19) and the lunges are 'the survival' at 'MAX' (D20, M20); the CONJUGATE draft is identical (M21:M24). The rule 'work 1RIR -> accessory 2RIR -> nuance MAX -> survival ALL' holds on Monday and Wednesday only. The effort word follows the exercise role, not the slot name.

Chains were listed as a dynamic-effort/speed method ('bands ~50 %, chains ~70 %' in L03, table 5.1 and the strength rules), with non-verbatim quotes '~50%'/'~70%'. In ALL ABOUT SQUATS chains are a loading tool: 'BOTTOM CHAINS' '*INTENSIONALLY SLOW YOU DOWN', 'Chains are designed for magnitude influence, loading.', 'Weght can be moderate around 70%'. Bands are the speed tool: 'Bands are designed for speed/velocity', 'Weight should be lower ranges around 50% so you can move fast'. STRENGTH-8 is consistent with this ('HEAVY CHAINED DEADLIFT' on the max-effort day H9, 'FAST BANDED DL' on the speed day H18; the draft's speed-day 'FAST CHAINED DL' CJ H22 was changed to banded in the product). Quotes made verbatim, chains removed from the speed method, and an open question added.

STRENGTH-12 load (5.2): '(OBSERVED weeks 1-7; % for weeks 8-12 INFERRED)'. The % row is filled only for weeks 1-6 (O3:T3); U3 holds the text 'MID DELOAD' and V3:Z3 are blank. RPE is observed for all 12 weeks. Fixed.

BASEBALL deload (rule 7, D4, L06, PRE_8 week 8, open question 7): the 'DELOAD WEEK' was described as 'the same template'/'same exercises'. Read cell by cell, it replays the 'WEEK 7' grid (CL43:DC58), not 'WEEK 8'. It copies many exercises unchanged ('step to chest pass', 'single leg hops', 'lay down MB presses', 'camporini deadlift', 'OH rope tricep extension', 'seal DB row'), strips the intensified versions ('banded front squats' -> 'goblet squats', 'banded kb swings' -> 'kb swings', complex -> 'front squats', 'weighted Pull ups or max reps Close grip cable lat pull down' -> 'Close grip cable lat pull down', 'heavy DB step ups ' -> ' DB step ups ') and removes 'myo set' / 'myo sets'. This generator-relevant rule was missing; it was added.

Rule 11 / R12 / L08 / lever matrix said intensification methods are concentrated in the conversion/pre-season phases and are 'rare' in-season. BASEBALL writes upper-body 'Superset - same reps' / 'Superset - max reps' pairs and banded lifts in all three blocks: Block 1 week 1 (C34), in-season Block 3 (C70, AQ69 'SUPER SET 4X', DK68 'FAST BANDED DEADLFTS'). Only the '5 of each' complexes and 'myo set' / 'myo sets' are confined to Block 2. Fixed (matrix ATH_IN: 'S(supersets, bands)').

Rule 10 / R11 said the slot skeleton 'never changes inside a plan'. It changes at phase boundaries: BOXING week 3 replaces the whole menu (the Tuesday/Friday upper days dissolve into mixed sessions); AESTHETICS-12 drops the Monday/Thursday 'TRICEP EXT.' rows after weeks 7/8 and rebuilds Friday ('RFE Lunges (bulgarian)', 'Staggered stance unilateral deadlifts', one-leg extensions/curls, leg-press MYO). Reworded to 'held inside a phase'.

Rule 13 / R9 / L01 / governor modifier / open question 12 said in-season sets are 'frozen (4 per Part)'. Only Part C/D are 4 in Block 3; Part A is 1-3 sets (mostly 3) and Part B (core) 2-4 sets or 'Accumulate' time blocks. Fixed.

BASEBALL 'partC_D_sets' said '5 in Block 2 wk6-WEEK 8'. In 'wk 6' only Monday Part C is 5 (BW52); 'WEEK 7' is 5 everywhere; 'WEEK 8' is 5 except Friday Part D (DR54 = 4); Block 1 wk7 Monday Part D is 5 (DC37). Fixed; PRE_8 week 7 now notes Friday Part D 4.

CrossFit year (2.2, OBS_CF_MACRO): the day grids were not checked against the macro. The MARCH grid schedules STRENGTH ('KNEE DOM'/'PULL'/'HIP DOM'/'PUSH') and POWER ('SNATCH'/'CLEAN') days with no level, although the macro gives MARCH resistance only. changes.change: Every training block is a STAIRWAY: gradual weekly steps, smaller in the first half, a little bigger after the halfway point ('but not too much'), hardest weeks last, for every plan length. 12-week: HARDEST = the last 4 weeks (9-12, 'brutal'); 8-week: the same stairway (the v1 '4 adapting + 4 driving' split and the x1.10 'start hard' are retired). Planned steps (PROPOSED numbers, the same as 12_volume_algorithm v1.1 §3.7.1, which owns the set math): 3 % to the halfway week, 5 % after; when a muscle's cap would come early, all its steps shrink by one factor λ so the peak lands on the cap in the last week (12-week λ: L1 0.76, L2 0.87, L3 0.50); older adults (60+) at most 3 %; nothing above 7 % is ever planned.

'Start at a 2, end at an 11' is how hard the week feels (overall volume and loading), not a set count: week 1 feels like a 2, the last week like an 11 ('a little bit past your limits'). Every week at least one dial climbs (a set, load or reps, or the RIR target); a 2-11 'stair level' is printed on each week (display PROPOSED). Advanced lifters at the set ceiling climb by heavier loads, intensifiers and a rotating priority muscle (approved proposal).

No check-in = no adaptation: the plan runs its planned stairway unchanged ('There is no data to go off of'). The v1 intake-based starting rate (3 % for stress, short sleep, physical job, 60+, layoff or pain; 'target-seeking' smallest rate) is retired: nothing in the stairway depends on sleep, stress or life.

The optional weekly check-in picks the step from EFFORT, COMPLETION and PAIN only (the approved step table without its 'life' column; RESOLUTION FLAGGED, see below): on target (7-8) = the planned step; too easy (mostly 1-6) = the planned step + 2 points (never above 7 %); 9 = hold; any 10 ('the max I could do, but successful') = hold and -1 set on that day; under half the sessions = repeat the week; pain = pain protocol. A separate 'failed' option may sit next to 10. The v1 readiness score (with a 0.20 life weight) is retired.

No deload or maintenance week inside a block: blocks are completed. The v1 triggered mid-block deload (D6) is retired; its signals now only OFFER 'cancel this block' and the person or coach decides. Cancel -> maintenance phase -> a whole new block from week 1.

Between two completed blocks: one recovery week at about half the sets of the hardest week, same exercises, 3+ RIR (approved: 'week 1 of the next cycle is a deload'). It sits between the blocks and does not shorten the next block's stairway (counting PROPOSED; 14.3 #2); none after a maintenance phase. A maintenance phase at the end of a block only when the person or coach asks for it.

Maintenance phase: the user picks its length (default 4 weeks) and can add weeks; at its end the plan stops and asks 'Keep maintaining / change your plan / start a training block'. Dose stays 50-70 % of the last block's final 4 weeks (PER-01) and is not floored: the floor of 10 sets (R2-VOL-06 'I don't think anybody needs less than 10') applies to training blocks, not to maintenance (12_volume_algorithm v1.1 §3.3; 14.3 #4).

Next block after a COMPLETED block: start x1.05, cap +1 set (never above 25; priority 30), all customizable (approved). After a CANCELLED block: the same start. While 1-2 priority muscles are pushed, the others grow at most 3 %/week (approved).

Pre-season = the 4-6-week 'season change' maintenance-type block: about 60 % of the off-season's sets (flat), more speed and power, ending with a 1-2-week taper before the first game (approved); its length can be changed. The tool works out off-, pre- and in-season from the season start date plus practice and game days.

Receive-Create stages approved: RC1 Land -> RC2 Land & Go -> RC3 Repeat. 12-week: weeks 1-3 / 4-7 / 8-12; 8-week: 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8; restart at RC1 each off-season; stay put in maintenance blocks (pre-season included); intermediate and advanced athletes may start at RC2. (v1 used 1-2 / 3-5 / 6+.)

Olympic lifts: up to 4 days a week; clean-family days count as squat-pattern (knee-dominant) days and snatch-family days as hinge-pattern days ('snatches a little bit more hingy than squatty'; OBSERVED basis: BASEBALL Block 2 Mon/Thu cleans, Tue/Fri snatches). In-season a light 2 x 3 piece (hang power clean or DB snatch), dropped in heavy game weeks. Full squat cleans/snatches 3-5 reps per set at the same weekly reps; DB/KB and hang-pull variants keep the 4 x 8 -> 4 x 4 ramp. Weight by RIR/RPE and bar speed ('these are for power output'); % only with a tested max of that exact lift; competitive weightlifters get their own programming. 60+: none by default (an option, with a warning); youth from the floor from about 14 after a hang block.

In-season, game-heavy sports (basketball, volleyball, soccer, football, hockey): gym plyos at about half, no extra change-of-direction work, sprints only for speed athletes, and the one hard gym day at least 48 h before a game (approved).

Plyo:ballistic shares approved (plyometric share of jump and throw work at the END of a block: sprinters 75 %; volleyball, soccer, football skill 60 %; basketball, tennis, football big-skill, weekend warriors 50 %; baseball, softball, hockey, linemen, MMA 40 %; boxing, karate, kickboxing, wrestling, BJJ, golf 25 %); each block starts 15 points more ballistic. Ballistic vs plyometric jump lists approved.

Aerobic sessions approved: athletes off-season 2-4 by sport (baseball, softball, sprinters 2; basketball, volleyball, football, tennis, golf, boxing, BJJ 3; soccer, hockey, kickboxing, karate 3-4; MMA, wrestling 4), pre-season 2, in-season 2 (ATH-07), powerlifters 2 easy (Orange); aesthetics 4 including a second easy Orange, plus optional walks. Every count can be moved up or down by the user.

The yearly plan is approved as the GEN-POP 'stay in shape' plan: Jan-Mar hard work + more cardio, start cutting, sets stay at the starting level; Apr-Jun summer shape (keep losing fat while building a little muscle); Jul-Sep maintain at about 70 %; Oct-mid-Dec build muscle, less cardio; last 2 weeks of December automatic maintenance. Summer follows the user's hemisphere; users mark their own holiday and vacation weeks (they switch to maintenance); everything is tunable (re-order or change blocks, more or less cardio, e.g. a winter powerlifting-style block). Athletes follow their season instead.

Testing: before the block (or in week 1) and at the end (last week, instead of that week's top sets), never during the block. Anyone who has not completed a training block tests submaximally (5RM or 3RM; cardio and speed at 80-90 % effort), never a 1RM or a max-effort mile from zero. Menu and reminders (block start, 7 days and 1 day before) approved. The '21.6 mile run' is removed from plans and tests.

Spine: heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days; non-axial hinge, leg press or belt squat on the other lower days; the counted list of axial lifts is approved. This replaces v1's 'squat once a week'.

Session rules carried into the overlays: core opens light (2 exercises x 2 sets, short of failure) and core supersets or monster sets may be added anywhere; field athletes up to 12 exercises + the 2-exercise core block; full-body days use 2-4 exercises per muscle (never 1), so they can run longer.

Between exercise blocks the plan may change ONE detail of a library exercise (hand, grip, stance, implement, range), shown as e.g. 'Reverse lunge - dumbbell in opposite hand'; it never invents an exercise.

Every popular US sport, swimming included, is mapped to a season type (game-heavy team, diamond, meet/championship with a taper, combat with a date, tournament, event race, strength/physique meet, seasonal outdoor) with its periodization rules. Gen-pop 'stay athletic and active' (pickleball, HYROX and other recreational activities) gets the weekend-warrior athletic overlay inside the gen-pop stairway or year, play days handled like practice/game days, and an optional event date with a 1-week taper. Per-sport numbers live in 04_profiles v1.1.
The sample plans he will grade are mapped to their mode and skeleton: swimming, football, soccer, CrossFit-style bootcamp, bootcamp, full-body aesthetics, push/pull/legs.

Weight guidance: reps-in-reserve language with the week-1 tip ('pick a weight you could lift 2-3 more times'); % only for barbell main lifts with a recent tested best and for Olympic lifts with a tested max of that lift.

headline_rules: R1 Plan modes chosen at intake: 12-week block (his preferred), 8-week block, maintenance phase (length chosen) and the yearly gen-pop plan; prep (event / fight / meet date) and season (competitive athlete) are overlays. No 6-week loading plan. The week-by-week mode is retired with the check-ins. (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; COACH-R2 R2-PER-01, R2-PER-06; COACH-R3 R3-VOL-02, R3-VOL-04)

R2 The generator outputs the whole plan once, with its built-in stairway: no check-ins, no tracking, no adaptive inputs and nothing stored; the person or coach sees every week ahead and adjusts the plan themselves (switch off a day's athletic or core block, add or remove exercises or blocks; supersets recommended). (COACH-R3 R3-VOL-02, R3-VOL-04, R3-GEN-01, R3-SES-02)

R3 Every training block is a stairway: gradual weekly steps, smaller in the first weeks, a little bigger after the halfway point 'but not too much', hardest weeks last; 12-week: the last 4 weeks (9-12) are 'brutal'; every plan length. (COACH-R2 R2-PER-03, R2-PER-04; approved COACH-R3 R3-VOL-04)

R4 'Start at a 2, end at an 11' is how hard the week feels (overall volume and loading), not a set count; every week at least one dial climbs: a set, load or reps, or the RIR target. (COACH-R2 R2-PER-05; dial rule PROPOSED)

R5 Planned steps (approved): about 3 % a week to the halfway week, about 5 % after; when a group's cap would come early, all its steps shrink by one factor λ so each trained group reaches its ceiling in the last week; older adults (60+) run the same steps (the v1.1 PROPOSED <= 3 % cap is retired, as in 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.4: it would keep them from reaching the ceiling in the last week; they are protected by the R3-ATH-02 defaults and constrained machines, EQ-03); never above 7 %; the person's total weekly sets rise < 10 %. Phases: 12-week ACCLIMATION 1-3 (L1 1-4, L3 1-2) -> DRIVE to week 8 -> HARDEST 9-12; 8-week ACCLIMATION 1-2 (L1 1-3, L3 1) -> DRIVE to week 5 -> HARDEST 6-8. (COACH-R3 R3-VOL-04; COACH-R2 R2-PER-03, R2-PER-04; COACH-ANSWER PER-01, UNI-05)

R6 Counting on focus groups: hips = glutes + hamstrings (e.g. RDL + hip thrust + leg curl = 3 hip exercises), shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor; users and coaches can add more rear-delt work); 2-4 exercises per group trained that day; calves one exercise x 3 sets per leg day; Focus muscle 1 / 2 (optional, max 2) get +1 to +3 weekly sets each inside the stairway (COACH-R3 R3-SES-01, R3-VOL-01); time vs minimums: when the chosen days and minutes cannot hold the minimums, the plan (1) says so up front and offers another day or longer sessions, (2) if the time stays, trains fewer groups directly (big movers first; arms, calves and shoulder isolation from compound credit) instead of every group under the floor, (3) recommends supersets, and (4) keeps the stairway climbing on the groups it trains - never flat (COACH-R3 R3-SES-02; algorithm in 12_volume_algorithm / 05 v1.2).

R7 No deload or maintenance week inside a block: blocks are completed. A person or coach who cannot complete a block stops it -> maintenance phase -> a whole new block from week 1; a holiday marked after the start also ends the block unless the mark is removed. (COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07; COACH-R3 R3-PER-01)

R8 After a completed block the block just ends; an easy week at about half the sets of the hardest week (same exercises, 3+ RIR) is RECOMMENDED, not mandatory, as an extra week (12 + 1 = 13); the user goes back into the app and builds what comes next. (COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07; COACH-R3 R3-PER-01; COACH-ANSWER PER-05)

R9 Maintenance phase: length chosen (default 4 weeks); 50-70 % of the last block's final 4 weeks (not floored), RIR 2-3, no intensifiers; when it ends the plan ends and the user builds the next plan (keep maintaining, change the plan or start a block). (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; COACH-R2 R2-PER-06; COACH-R3 R3-PER-01; factor split PROPOSED)

R10 Next block after a completed one: start x1.05, cap +1 set (max 25, priority 30), customizable; advanced lifters at the ceiling climb by load, intensifiers and a rotating priority muscle; after a stopped block the same start. Nothing is stored, so the intake asks 'Did you just finish a block?' and how many in a row (0 by default; 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.12): x1.05 and cap +1 per completed block (PROPOSED). (COACH-R2 R2-VOL-06, R2-PER-05; COACH-R3 R3-GEN-01)

R11 Exercises stay fixed inside 4-6-week exercise blocks; between them 1-2 one-detail variations of library exercises, never invented ones; A/B lead-lift weeks only for variety seekers; heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days. (COACH-ANSWER PER-02, PER-03; COACH-R2 R2-LIB-01, R2-SES-01, R2-SES-02)

R12 Tests: before the block (or in week 1) and in the last week, never during the block; anyone without a completed block tests submaximally (5RM / 3RM, 80-90 % efforts), never a 1RM or a max-effort mile from zero; the test days and 'get ready' lines are printed in the plan (nothing stored). (COACH-R2 R2-PER-07; COACH-R3 R3-GEN-01)

R13 Yearly plan (gen-pop 'stay in shape'): Q1 hard work + more cardio, start cutting, sets at the starting level; Q2 summer shape; Q3 maintain at ~70 %; Q4 build muscle, less cardio; last 2 weeks of December holiday maintenance, printed by default and, like every maintenance week, a recommendation the user can switch off (R3-PER-01); user's hemisphere; holiday weeks planned between blocks; the easy weeks after the Q1 and Q2 blocks are recommendations; fully tunable. Athletes follow their season. (COACH-R2 R2-PER-01, R2-PER-02; COACH-R3 R3-PER-01)

R14 Competitive athletes: season start date + practice / game days -> off-season (stairway blocks, VOL 1 -> 2 -> 3), pre-season (4-6 weeks at ~60 % with speed / power and a 1-2-week taper), in-season (2 gym days, low volume; game-heavy sports - basketball, volleyball, soccer, football, hockey (R2-ATH-07) and lacrosse, field hockey, rugby, ultimate, flag football, beach volleyball (COACH-R3 R3-ATH-04) - plyos ~half, no extra COD, sprints only for speed athletes, hard day >= 48 h before a game), post-season recovery. (COACH-ANSWER PER-08, PER-11; COACH-R2 R2-GEN-05, R2-PER-06, R2-ATH-07; COACH-R3 R3-ATH-04)

R15 Athletic work has its own budget; Receive-Create stages RC1 Land -> RC2 Land & Go -> RC3 Repeat (12-week 1-3 / 4-7 / 8-12; 8-week 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8; restart each off-season; hold in maintenance); end-of-block plyo shares by sport (round-2 list + the remaining sports approved in round 3), each block starting 15 points more ballistic; recreational players use their activity's share. (COACH-ANSWER VOL-10, CAT-10; COACH-R2 R2-ATH-01, R2-ATH-03; COACH-R3 R3-ATH-04)

R16 Olympic lifts for everyone in athletic training, up to 4 days a week (clean days = squat pattern, snatch days = hinge pattern); weight by RIR/RPE and speed unless a tested max; full lifts 3-5 reps per set; in-season a light 2 x 3, dropped in heavy game weeks; 60+: landing drills (step down and stick, no bounce), balance, quick stepping without a hop, light medball throws and fast machine work ON; low ankle hops, other jumps, Olympic lifts and depth jumps OFF and switchable with the warning 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means'; overhead and low-bar squats out; snatch variants out (EQ-03) (COACH-R2 R2-ATH-08; COACH-R3 R3-ATH-02); youth from the floor from ~14 after a hang block. (COACH-ANSWER ATH-10; COACH-R2 R2-ATH-04, R2-ATH-05, R2-ATH-08, R2-GEN-06; COACH-R3 R3-ATH-02)

R17 Effort stays inside 1-3 RIR (approved drift): 3 RIR early (the '2'), 2 RIR after halfway, 1-2 RIR in the last weeks and 1 RIR plus intensifiers (MYO, supersets; MAX only on small-muscle or bodyweight work) in the final week (the '11'); never to failure on heavy compounds. (COACH-ANSWER VOL-13, GEN-08; COACH-R2 R2-PER-05; COACH-R3 R3-VOL-04)

R18 Swimming (season type C): 3 dryland days + 1 optional (2 for younger or lower-level swimmers), 0 extra gym cardio, jumps mostly ballistic (25 % plyometric), Olympic lifts 2-3 days, shoulder care every session without bands; swimmers: a 2-week dryland taper lined up with the swim coach's taper before the main championship meet; 1 week or none before smaller meets. (COACH-R3 R3-ATH-01)

R19 Stay athletic and active (gen pop): the weekend-warrior athletic overlay inside the gen-pop stairway or year; play days (approved, COACH-R3 R3-ATH-05): the user can enter the days they play; the hardest gym day stays at least 48 h before the biggest play day; weeks with 3+ play sessions drop the extra agility drills and half the jumps; a 45-60+ minute session of the activity counts as one of the 3 cardio sessions, up to 2 (COACH-R3 R3-ATH-05); optional event date for gen pop (a first HYROX race, a pickleball tournament, a 10K): the hardest weeks end 1 week before, then 1 easy week at about half the sets (intensity kept); no date -> the normal stairway or year; after the event the plan ends and the user builds the next (R3-PER-01); HYROX (approved, COACH-R3 R3-ATH-03): 2 strength days (squat + pull, deadlift + push) + 2 hybrid days (run intervals, or 1 km run + 1 station repeated); 4 cardio sessions (Blue, Green, Orange + a second Orange) because running is about half the race; 2 short station circuits a week (sled push / pull, burpee broad jumps, wall balls, farmers carry, sandbag lunges, SkiErg / row) as finishers that never count as muscle sets; wall balls with the race ball (never over 20 lb); 40-rep / AMRAP sets only inside these circuits; jumps 50 % plyometric; pickleball, padel and tennis players 50+: knee-friendly strength, calf and Achilles work every leg day, rotator-cuff work, only low-impact jumps (no depth jumps, hurdle hops or bounds) unless switched on (COACH-R3 R3-ATH-02). (COACH-R3 R3-ATH-02, R3-ATH-03, R3-ATH-05; COACH-ANSWER ATH-13)

strength_template_8wk_v1_1.sets_x_reps: 7 x 2 @ ~95 %, or the test if ticked

olympic_v1_1.frequency: up to 4 days a week ('it could be done four times a week'); clean-family days count as squat-pattern (knee-dominant) days, snatch-family days as hinge-pattern (hip-dominant) days ('I take snatches a little bit more hingy than squatty'). OBSERVED basis: BASEBALL Block 2 'wk 5' runs the OLY piece on Mon/Thu (cleans) and Tue/Fri (snatches); HYBRID-8 cleans Monday, snatch Thursday.
olympic_v1_1.frequency_tag: COACH-R2 R2-ATH-04; OBSERVED BASEBALL Block 2, HYBRID-8
olympic_v1_1.load: by RIR/RPE and bar speed ('these are for power output'): pick weights that stay fast, stop the set when the speed drops (coach's eye, R2-ATH-05); the % ramp (75 -> 80 -> 85 -> 90 %) only when the person has a tested max of that exact lift (R2-ATH-05); competitive Olympic weightlifters need their own programming (R2-GEN-06).
olympic_v1_1.reps: DB/KB and hang-pull/hang-power variants keep the 4 x 8 -> 4 x 6 -> 4 x 6 -> 4 x 4 ramp; full squat cleans and snatches 3-5 reps per set at the same weekly reps (e.g. 6 x 5 instead of 4 x 8).
olympic_v1_1.in_season: a light piece, 2 sets of 3 (hang power clean or DB snatch), 1-2 days; dropped in heavy game weeks.
olympic_v1_1.older: 60+: no Olympic lifts by default; available as an option with the warning 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means.'
olympic_v1_1.youth: from the floor from about 14 years, after one block of hang work.
olympic_v1_1.tags: COACH-ANSWER ATH-10, PER-09, LIB-07; COACH-R2 R2-ATH-04, R2-ATH-05, R2-ATH-08, R2-GEN-06
olympic_v1_1.older_v1_2: 60+: landing drills (step down and stick, no bounce), balance, quick stepping without a hop, light medball throws and fast machine work ON; low ankle hops, other jumps, Olympic lifts and depth jumps OFF and switchable with the warning 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means'; overhead and low-bar squats out; snatch variants out (EQ-03) (COACH-R2 R2-ATH-08; COACH-R3 R3-ATH-02)

intensity_model.effort_v1_1_note: RIR is the effort language: 1-3 RIR at all times (VOL-13); the stair runs from RIR 3 in week 1 (a '2') to RIR 1 with MAX/MYO on small-muscle or bodyweight work in the last week (an '11') (R2-PER-05); never to failure on heavy compounds (GEN-08); effort 10 = 'the max I could do, but successful', a separate 'failed' option may exist (R2-VOL-02); weight by RIR/RPE with the week-1 tip, % only with a recent tested best (R2-GEN-06).
intensity_model.effort_v1_2_note: v1.2: the RIR drift is approved (3 RIR early -> 2 -> 1-2 -> 1 + intensifiers in the last week, always inside 1-3 RIR; R3-VOL-04); no effort ratings are collected and nothing reacts to them (R3-VOL-02); the v1.1 note about the check-in menu is history

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Easy (recovery) week after a COMPLETED block = about HALF the sets of the hardest (last) week (round up, min 1 per exercise), the same exercises, lighter load or 3+ RIR, no buy-outs, finishers, MYO or supersets. Athletic work: landings / low amplitude at about half the contacts and throws; conditioning easy (Orange) only. It is a RECOMMENDATION, not mandatory: the plan prints it after the block and the person may skip it.
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-05; COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07 (dose approved); COACH-R3 R3-PER-01 (an extra week, a recommendation); MYO/superset removal and athletic/conditioning parts PROPOSED
deload_test_taper_rules.v1: Deload = about HALF the sets of the current week (round up, minimum 1 per exercise), the same exercises, lighter load or 3+ RIR, no buy-outs, finishers, MYO or supersets. Athletic work: landings / low amplitude at about half the contacts and throws; conditioning easy (Orange) only.
deload_test_taper_rules.v1_1: Recovery (deload) week = about HALF the sets of the hardest (last) week (round up, min 1 per exercise), the same exercises, lighter load or 3+ RIR, no buy-outs, finishers, MYO or supersets. Athletic work: landings / low amplitude at about half the contacts and throws; conditioning easy (Orange) only.

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: 12-week block: NO deload or maintenance week inside. The recommended easy week sits after week 12 and before the next block's week 1 as an EXTRA week (the next block keeps all 12 stairway weeks; 12 + 1 = a 13-week quarter in the year plan). When the block ends it ends: the plan stops there and the user builds the next block in the app. No easy week when a maintenance phase follows or precedes.
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07 ('It should never be thrown in the middle of a block'); COACH-R3 R3-PER-01 (approved: extra week; 'maintenance weeks are a recommendation')
deload_test_taper_rules.v1: 12-week cycle: no deload at a fixed week. A deload happens when the logs trigger it (D6), and the first week of the NEXT cycle is a deload (skip it when a maintenance block came between).
deload_test_taper_rules.v1_1: 12-week block: NO deload or maintenance week inside. One recovery week sits after week 12 and before the next block's week 1 (the approved 'week 1 of the next cycle is a deload', counted as an extra week so the next block keeps its 12 stairway weeks). No recovery week when a maintenance phase follows or precedes.

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: 8-week block: same as D2 (nothing inside; the recommended easy week after week 8 when the user builds another block).
deload_test_taper_rules.v1: 8-week plan: no planned deload inside (it 'starts hard' and drives weeks 5-8); triggered deloads only; the next plan opens with a deload or a maintenance block.
deload_test_taper_rules.v1_1: 8-week block: same as D2 (nothing inside; one recovery week after week 8 when another block follows).

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Maintenance phase for: a block the person or coach stops; the end of a block when the person or coach wants it (a recommendation, never forced); vacation, travel, moving; user-marked holiday weeks; the last 2 weeks of December (printed by default; a recommendation, R3-PER-01); year Q3; the athlete's season change (pre-season, D8). The user picks its length (default 4 weeks). When it ends, the plan ends and the user builds what comes next in the app - keep maintaining, change the plan or start a training block (his R2-PER-06 options). Volume 50-70 % of the last block's final 4 weeks (50 % vacation/limited equipment, 60 % travel/moving/season change, 70 % planned maintenance and year Q3; older adults >= 70 %), not floored (the floor of 10 is for training blocks); flat; RIR 2-3; no intensifiers; loads kept, sets cut. Afterwards a whole new block from week 1.
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-01 (50-70 %, uses); COACH-R2 R2-PER-06 (length chosen), R2-VOL-07, R2-PER-01 (Q3 ~70 %); COACH-R3 R3-PER-01 (recommendation; the plan ends and the user builds the next); factor split and older floor PROPOSED; floor reading as 12_volume_algorithm v1.2
deload_test_taper_rules.v1: A 4-6-week maintenance/transition block replaces loading when life needs it: vacation (1-2 weeks inside it), travel, moving, season change (off -> in), or planned maintenance. Volume about 50-70 % of the last block (50 % vacation/limited equipment, 60 % travel/moving/season change, 70 % planned maintenance; older adults >= 70 %), rate 0, RIR 2-3, no intensifiers; keep the loads, cut the sets.
deload_test_taper_rules.v1_1: Maintenance phase for: a cancelled block; the end of a block when the person or coach asks; vacation, travel, moving; user-marked holiday weeks; the automatic last 2 weeks of December; year Q3; the athlete's season change (pre-season, D8). The user picks its length (default 4 weeks) and can add weeks; at its end the plan stops and asks 'Keep maintaining / Change your plan / Start a training block' (no answer -> keep maintaining, PROPOSED). Volume 50-70 % of the last block's final 4 weeks (50 % vacation/limited equipment, 60 % travel/moving/season change, 70 % planned maintenance and year Q3; older adults >= 70 %), not floored (the floor of 10 is for training blocks); flat; RIR 2-3; no intensifiers; loads kept, sets cut. Afterwards a whole new block from week 1.

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Vacation and holiday weeks are maintenance weeks (50 % with what is available, or full rest). They are planned BETWEEN blocks. If the user marks one after a block has started, that block ends there (stop -> maintenance -> a new block) unless they remove the mark. Return: a new block at the previous start.
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-01; COACH-R2 R2-PER-02, R2-VOL-07; COACH-R3 R3-PER-01 (approved); SCIENCE Hwang 2017, Bosquet 2013
deload_test_taper_rules.v1: Vacation of 1-2 weeks: train at ~50 % with what is available (bodyweight, hotel gym), or rest completely; return at the previous start (no opening deload, no level step).
deload_test_taper_rules.v1_1: Vacation and holiday weeks are maintenance weeks (50 % with what is available, or full rest). Planned ahead: the planner places them between blocks. Marked after a block has started and inside it: that block ends early (D6 flow) unless the user removes the mark. Return: a new block at the previous start.

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: No triggered deload and no automatic 'stop' offer: the v1.1 block-at-risk prompt read check-in signals, and check-ins are retired (R3-PER-01 item 3 lapses with them). The person or coach can stop a block at any time (their call): stop -> maintenance phase (D4) -> a whole new block from week 1 at the same start. Inside the block they may lighten a day themselves (switch off the athletic or core block, remove a set or an exercise); the printed stairway does not change.
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07 ('If they can't complete it, they should cancel the block and start a maintenance phase'); COACH-R3 R3-VOL-02, R3-VOL-04, R3-PER-01, R3-SES-02
deload_test_taper_rules.v1: Early (unplanned) deload when: 2 weeks of hold in a row; median EFFORT >= 9 two weeks in a row; 'Felt a PAIN' on 2+ slots in one week; or performance down on 3+ main lifts for 2 exposures. After it, resume at the volume of 2 weeks before.
deload_test_taper_rules.v1_1: No triggered deload (the v1 D6 is retired). The plan shows a block-at-risk prompt ('continue the block' or 'cancel it and start a maintenance phase'; it never inserts lighter weeks by itself) when, with check-ins: 2 hold weeks in a row; effort mostly 9-10 two weeks in a row; under half the sessions 2 weeks running; 'Felt a PAIN' on 2+ exercises in one week; or the person taps 'I can't keep up'. The person or coach decides: continue (holds and repeated weeks are allowed) or cancel -> maintenance phase (D4) -> a whole new block from week 1 at the same start. Without check-ins there are no signals and the block runs as planned.

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Tests are ticked at the start of the block (or 'No need for testing'). Baseline before the block or in week 1 (week 1 is the light '2' week); end test in the last week, replacing that week's top sets; the rest of that week at about 50-70 % of its sets. Never during the block. Anyone who has not completed a training block (new, untrained, or back after 6+ months off) tests submaximally: 5RM or 3RM for strength, 80-90 % efforts for cardio and speed; never a 1RM or a max-effort mile from zero. The previous block's end test is the next block's baseline (the user enters it; nothing is stored). Test days and 'get ready' lines are printed in the plan.
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-07; COACH-R2 R2-PER-07 (before + end only; submax from zero; menu approved); COACH-R3 R3-GEN-01 (nothing stored); rest-of-week dose and baseline reuse PROPOSED; SCIENCE Reynolds 2006, Pritchard 2016
deload_test_taper_rules.v1: Tests are chosen by checkbox at the start of the block, or 'No need for testing'. The test day sits in the last week of the block and replaces that week's top sets; the rest of that week runs at about 50-70 % of its sets. Reminders before the test (section 6.1).
deload_test_taper_rules.v1_1: Tests are ticked at the start of the block (or 'No need for testing'). Baseline before the block or in week 1 (week 1 is the light '2' week); end test in the last week, replacing that week's top sets; the rest of that week at about 50-70 % of its sets. Never during the block. Anyone who has not completed a training block (new, untrained, or back after 6+ months off) tests submaximally: 5RM or 3RM for strength, 80-90 % efforts for cardio and speed; never a 1RM or a max-effort mile from zero. The previous block's end test is the next block's baseline.

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Taper = the last 1-2 weeks before a season opener, event or fight: volume about -40-60 % (progressive), intensity and frequency kept, no new exercises. Athletes: inside the 4-6-week pre-season block (1 week for a 4-5-week pre-season, 2 weeks for 6). Swimmers: a 2-week dryland taper lined up with the swim coach's taper before the main championship meet; 1 week or none before smaller meets. Gen-pop events (a first HYROX race, a pickleball tournament, a 10K): the hardest weeks end 1 week before, then 1 easy week at about half the sets. After the event the plan ends and the user builds the next.
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-R2 R2-PER-06 ('ending with a 1-2-week taper before the first game'); COACH-ANSWER PER-08; COACH-R3 R3-ATH-01, R3-ATH-05 (approved), R3-PER-01; SCIENCE Bosquet 2007, Pritchard 2016, Vachon 2020, Aouani 2024
deload_test_taper_rules.v1: Before a season opener, event or fight: 1-2 weeks, volume -40-60 % (progressive), intensity and frequency kept, no new exercises.
deload_test_taper_rules.v1_1: Taper = the last 1-2 weeks before a season opener, event or fight: volume about -40-60 % (progressive), intensity and frequency kept, no new exercises. Athletes: inside the 4-6-week pre-season block (1 week for a 4-5-week pre-season, 2 weeks for 6). Swimmers' main championship meet: 2 weeks of dryland taper lined up with the pool taper (PROPOSED, 14.3 #6). Gen-pop events (HYROX race, tournament, 10K): 1 week.

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Post-season / end of a throwing block: a recovery week that is not a scaled copy (arm care, mobility, easy aerobic, no main lifts), then general work or a maintenance phase (a recommendation, R3-PER-01) before the next off-season.
deload_test_taper_rules.v1: Post-season / end of a throwing block: a recovery week that is not a scaled copy (arm care, mobility, easy aerobic, no main lifts), then general work before the next off-season.

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: Year plan: the last 2 weeks of December are printed as maintenance by default (about 60 %, 50-70 %), any equipment, RIR 2-3; like every maintenance week it is a recommendation, not mandatory - the user can switch it off (R3-PER-01); January starts the Q1 block at week 1. User-marked holiday and vacation weeks (Christmas, Semana Santa, Thanksgiving, a trip) switch to maintenance too and are planned between blocks (D5).
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-01; COACH-R2 R2-PER-01, R2-PER-02; COACH-R3 R3-PER-01; 60 % default PROPOSED; SCIENCE Yanovski 2000, Diaz-Zavala 2017
deload_test_taper_rules.v1: Yearly mode: the last 2 weeks of December switch automatically to maintenance (about 50-70 %; default 60 %), any equipment, RIR 2-3; January restarts at the previous start.
deload_test_taper_rules.v1_1: Year plan: the last 2 weeks of December switch automatically to maintenance (about 60 %, 50-70 %), any equipment, RIR 2-3; January starts the Q1 block at week 1. User-marked holiday and vacation weeks (Christmas, Semana Santa, Thanksgiving, a trip) switch to maintenance too and are placed between blocks (D5).

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: In-season: no planned deload; sets flat (0 %); 2 gym days. Game-heavy sports - basketball, volleyball, soccer, football, hockey (R2-ATH-07) and lacrosse, field hockey, rugby, ultimate, flag football, beach volleyball (COACH-R3 R3-ATH-04): gym plyos about half, no extra change-of-direction work, sprints only for speed athletes, the one hard gym day at least 48 h before a game. Olympic piece light (2 x 3), dropped in heavy game weeks; a heavy game week (3+ games, or 2 + travel) keeps only the light day (PROPOSED).
deload_test_taper_rules.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-08, UNI-10; COACH-R2 R2-ATH-07, R2-ATH-04; COACH-R3 R3-ATH-04; heavy-week definition PROPOSED
deload_test_taper_rules.v1: In-season: no planned deload; rate 0; a lighter week around congested game/travel weeks.

deload_test_taper_rules.rule: After a COMPLETED block the next one starts one step up: start x1.05 and cap +1 set (never above 25; priority 30), all customizable; advanced lifters already at the ceiling climb by heavier loads, intensifiers (MYO, supersets) and a rotating priority muscle up to 30. Nothing is stored, so the intake asks 'Did you just finish a block?' and how many in a row (0 by default; 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.12), and starts one step up per completed block (PROPOSED). After a stopped block: the same start.

deload_test_taper_rules.v1: After a productive 12-week cycle the next one starts one level higher (start x 1.05, cap + 1 set; max 25 non-priority, 30 priority). After holds, pain or a maintenance block: same start.
deload_test_taper_rules.v1_1: After a COMPLETED block the next one starts one step up: start x1.05 and cap +1 set (never above 25; priority 30), all customizable; advanced lifters already at the ceiling climb by heavier loads, intensifiers (MYO, supersets) and a rotating priority muscle up to 30. After a CANCELLED block: the same start. A block whose last 4 weeks were mostly holds or ended with an open pain flag also repeats its start (PROPOSED).

season_calendar_v1_1.inputs: next season start date (first game) or 'in season until', plus practice days and game days per week (R2-GEN-05)
rule: In season now -> IN-SEASON until the 'in season until' date -> POST-SEASON 1-2 weeks -> OFF-SEASON.
W = weeks from the plan start to the first game. PRE-SEASON = the last 6 weeks (4 when W is 7-9), ending with the taper (1 week for 4-5 weeks, 2 for 6); W <= 6 -> pre-season only (W weeks).

OFF-SEASON = the weeks before the pre-season: 12-week block if >= 12 weeks remain (earlier weeks: a 4-8-week foundation block, or general/maintenance weeks if fewer than 4; L1-L2 athletes with >= 16 weeks may run STARTING -> MID -> ADVANCED as blocks, PRG-04 PROPOSED); 8-week block if 8-11 remain; a short 4-7-week stairway if 4-7 remain; 1-3 leftover weeks run as general weeks.
Off-season blocks are stairways with a recommended easy week between them (R3-PER-01); the pre-season starts right after the last off-season block (its lower volume is the unload).

v1.2: the season plan is printed once from these inputs - the off-season blocks and the pre-season to the first game (R3-VOL-04); when it ends the athlete builds the in-season plan in the app (R3-PER-01; PROPOSED reading)
