generator_pseudocode:
generate_plan(intake):                                   # v1.2 (round-3 answers applied): output only - no check-ins, nothing stored
  level  = level_from_experience(years, months_off, ex_pro)   # L1/L2/L3 (PRG-05)
  family = map_goal(goal)       # HYPERTROPHY | STRENGTH | FAT_LOSS | GENERAL (incl. 'stay athletic & active') | HYBRID | ATHLETE
  mode   = intake.plan_mode     # C12 | C8 | MAINT(weeks chosen) | YEAR ; overlays PREP(event / fight / meet date) | SEASON(season start, practice/game days)
                                # week-by-week retired (R3-VOL-02, R3-VOL-04, R3-GEN-01)
  tests  = intake.test_ticks    # strength / cardio / speed / jumps / body, or 'No need for testing' (R2-PER-07)
  focus  = intake.focus_muscles[:2]                          # Focus 1 / Focus 2: +1..+3 weekly sets each (R3-SES-01)
  # NO lifestyle inputs (R2-GEN-04); NO check-ins, logs or stored history (R3-VOL-02, R3-VOL-04, R3-GEN-01)

  if SEASON: phases = season_calendar(start_date, season_start, practice_days, game_days)   # R2-GEN-05, R2-PER-06 (8.2.0); one printed season plan
  if PREP and swimmer_main_meet: taper = 2 weeks aligned with the swim taper (1 or 0 before smaller meets)   # R3-ATH-01
  if PREP and genpop_event: hardest weeks end 1 week before; then 1 easy week at ~half the sets            # R3-ATH-05
  grid    = STAIRWAY_GRID[mode](level, q1_cut)   # week -> phase, planned step (approved R3-VOL-04), stair level 2..11, RIR drift, exercise block, RC stage
  overlay = FAMILY_OVERLAY[family]              # phase -> reps, effort, load, methods, laterality, conditioning, athletic content
  start   = volume_engine.start(level, family, season, focus, pain)   # 12_volume_algorithm v1.2: groups (hips, shoulders ...), floor 10 on trained groups
  n = intake.blocks_completed_in_a_row (0 by default): start *= 1.05**n; cap += n   (cap <= 25, Focus / priority 30)    # R2-VOL-06; asked because nothing is stored (R3-GEN-01; 12 v1.2 §3.12, PROPOSED)
  release = health check (or the coach's skip + warning) + 'use at your own risk' tick + terms + liability release, on every build and rebuild   # R3-GEN-01; DISCLAIMER.md / .es.md; nothing stored
  time_fit = volume_engine.fit_time(days, minutes)            # R3-SES-02: warn + offer -> fewer groups trained directly -> supersets -> stairway still climbs

  if tests: print baseline before the block or in week 1 (submax if no completed block)   # R2-PER-07
  for week in grid:                                        # never a deload or maintenance week inside (R2-VOL-07)
      step = week.planned_step                              # ~3 % to halfway, ~5 % after, x lambda so each trained group peaks on its cap (R3-VOL-04); the same steps at 60+ (cap retired, 12 v1.2)
      T = min(cap, T * (1 + step)); place whole sets while T - current >= 1, total rise < 10 %   # VOL-06, VOL-07, UNI-05 (12 v1.2)
      placement: alternate the added set between the two exposures of a day type; small-muscle extras -> bonus exercise on the optional day (R3-VOL-03)
      if no set released: raise load/reps or step the RIR target                   # every week climbs (R2-PER-05)
      apply overlay[week.phase] -> reps, RIR (3 -> 2 -> 1-2 -> 1 + intensifiers, R3-VOL-04), methods
      athletic block (own budget, optional/toggle): plyo share by sport (R2-ATH-01, R3-ATH-04); RC stage by week (R2-ATH-03);
          Olympic up to 4 days, clean = squat pattern, snatch = hinge pattern (R2-ATH-04/05);
          60+: landing drills, balance, quick stepping, light throws, fast machine work; jumps / Olympic / depth jumps only if switched on (R3-ATH-02)
          stay-active: hardest gym day >= 48 h before the biggest play day; 3+ play sessions -> no extra agility, half the jumps (R3-ATH-05)
      core block (optional/toggle); supersets recommended per eligible pair (R3-SES-02)
      if season phase == IN: 2 days; game-heavy rule (R2-ATH-07, R3-ATH-04); Olympic 2 x 3, none in heavy game weeks (R2-ATH-04)
      if week.exercise_block_boundary: one-detail changes (R2-LIB-01)
      if week.is_last and tests: end test replaces the top sets; 'get ready' lines printed 7 d and 1 d before   # R2-PER-07, R3-GEN-01
  print the whole plan; after the last week: 'This block is done. Recommended: an easy week (half the sets). Build your next block, a maintenance phase or another plan.'   # R3-PER-01
  # editing on the printed plan (R3-SES-02): switch off a day's athletic / core block, add or remove exercises or blocks, superset pairs

science.claim: Concentrated blocks: accumulation -> transmutation -> realization; residual training effects ~30 +/- 5 days for aerobic endurance and maximal strength, ~18 days anaerobic glycolytic, ~5 +/- 3 days explosive/speed qualities.
science.citation: Issurin VB. New horizons for the methodology and physiology of training periodization. Sports Med 2010;40(3):189-206 (summary source: Sportlyzer Academy 'Block Periodization')
science.maps_to: CROSSFIT macro (RES -> STR -> POW -> TEST); athlete OFF_12 (base/conversion -> intensification -> realization); short residuals for speed/power explain why the coach keeps plyos/throws in EVERY phase including in-season. v1: block durations accumulation 2-6 weeks, transmutation 2-4 fit his 4-week athlete blocks (VOL 1 -> 2 -> 3, PER-11).

science.claim: More weekly sets -> more hypertrophy with diminishing returns; counting indirect sets as 0.5 ('fractional') predicts outcomes best; strength shows stronger diminishing returns and benefits more from frequency.
science.citation: Pelland JC et al. The Resistance Training Dose Response: Meta-Regressions Exploring the Effects of Weekly Volume and Frequency on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains. Sports Med 2026;56(2):481-505 (online 2025).
science.maps_to: v1 counts helpers at 0.25 (COACH-ANSWER VOL-09); Pelland's 0.5 is stored for research comparison (12_volume_algorithm_v1); 15-20 / 20-25 bands (UNI-01).

science.claim: Graded dose-response: each additional weekly set ~ +0.37 % gain; 10+ sets/muscle/week trend best.
science.citation: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW. Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass. J Sports Sci 2017.
science.maps_to: floors (>= ~10 sets for growth muscles).

science.claim: 12-20 weekly sets per muscle may be an optimum standard; >20 not clearly better for quads/biceps (triceps responded to higher).
science.citation: Baz-Valle E et al. A Systematic Review of The Effects of Different Resistance Training Volumes on Muscle Hypertrophy. J Hum Kinet 2022.
science.maps_to: the coach's 15-20 band (UNI-01) sits inside 12-20; his 20-25 'growth' range is where only triceps showed extra benefit (12_volume_algorithm_v1 §2.2); level caps L2 22 / L3 25 (approved and customizable, COACH-R2 R2-VOL-06).

science.claim: Hypertrophy improves as sets end closer to failure; strength gains similar across a wide RIR range.
science.citation: Robinson ZP et al. Exploring the Dose-Response Relationship Between Estimated Resistance Training Proximity to Failure, Strength Gain, and Muscle Hypertrophy. Sports Med 2024.
science.maps_to: isolation 'MAX'/'ALL', compounds 1-2 RIR; strength waves can stay at RPE 7-9.

science.topic: Progressive overload by load or reps
science.claim: Progressing repetitions at a fixed load produced hypertrophy and strength similar to progressing load in trained lifters.
science.citation: Plotkin D et al. Progressive overload without progressing load? PeerJ 2022; also Chaves TS et al. Int J Sports Med 2024.
science.maps_to: supports progressing small-muscle work by reps (VOL-11: small muscles 12-30); 40-rep sets stay an AMRAP option only (VOL-11); the study used lower-body exercises, so it supports rep progression in general.

science.claim: Heavier loads (>80 %) maximise strength; multi-set prescriptions rank highest for hypertrophy; all loads build muscle.
science.citation: Currier BS et al. Resistance training prescription for muscle strength and hypertrophy in healthy adults: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis. Br J Sports Med 2023.
science.maps_to: strength family drives % to 80-95 %; hypertrophy family drives sets.

science.claim: Volume-equated: periodized > non-periodized for 1RM; undulating slightly better for strength in trained people; no hypertrophy difference.
science.citation: Moesgaard L et al. Effects of Periodization on Strength and Muscle Hypertrophy in Volume-Equated Resistance Training Programs: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Sports Med 2022.
science.maps_to: the coach's within-week undulation (BASEBALL speed/strength days; FAT BURN heavy Tue / light Fri; leg ext '6 & 6' Mon vs '20/20' Thu) is supported for strength; hypertrophy depends on volume, not the scheme.

science.claim: Best taper: ~2 weeks, volume reduced 41-60 % (progressive/exponential), intensity and frequency maintained.
science.citation: Bosquet L et al. Effects of tapering on performance: a meta-analysis. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2007; Wang Z et al. PLOS ONE 2023; Mujika I, Padilla S. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2003; Vachon A et al. Eur J Sport Sci 2020 (team sports: taper improves power, RSA, COD, VO2max).
science.maps_to: deload/taper depth: his v1 deload (about half the sets, PER-05) sits inside the 41-60 % taper range; pre-season ends with a taper (D8). v1.1: pre-season taper 1-2 weeks (R2-PER-06); swimming championship 2 weeks (PROPOSED). v1.2: swimming championship 2 weeks with the swim taper (R3-ATH-01) and gen-pop events 1 easy week (R3-ATH-05), both approved.

science.claim: Expert consensus: deload = period of reduced training stress to mitigate fatigue; commonly 5-7 days every 4-6 weeks, highly variable; usually cut volume more than intensity.
science.citation: Bell L et al. Integrating Deloading into Strength and Physique Sports Training Programmes: An International Delphi Consensus Approach. Sports Med Open 2023 (definition); Bell L, Nolan D, Immonen V, et al. Front Sports Act Living 2022, qualitative interviews with 18 strength/physique coaches (deloads typically every 4-6 weeks, about 1 week long; range from every few weeks to 6-12 weeks).
science.maps_to: v1: deload = about half the sets (PER-05); placement by triggers or week 1 of the next cycle (PROPOSED); deloads every 4-6(7) weeks in practice (open question on his 12-week shape). v1.1: he decided deloads are never inside a block (R2-VOL-07); one recovery week sits between blocks. v1.2: that easy week is a recommendation, not mandatory (R3-PER-01).

science.claim: MEV -> MAV -> MRV; mesocycles of 4-6 weeks start near MEV, add sets weekly, deload at ~50 % volume when MRV is reached. Landmarks from RP's own muscle guides (practitioner, not peer-reviewed; intermediate lifters): chest MEV 4-6 / MAV 6-16 / MRV 16-24; quads 4-6 / 6-14 / 14-18; biceps 8-10 / 14-20 / 20-26; triceps 4-6 / 6-16 / 16-20; calves 4-6 / 6-16 / 16-24; specialisation (MRV*P) up to 24-35. Back values are published only as an image and were not extracted.
science.citation: Israetel M et al. (Renaissance Periodization) muscle training-tips guides at rpstrength.com (chest, quad, biceps, triceps, calves); framework summary at arvo.guru (which gives no per-muscle numbers).
science.maps_to: v1: his 12-week shape (acclimation -> drive -> hardest, then deload or maintenance) is the RP mesocycle logic; RP adds ~1 set/muscle/week, his person-level 3/5/7 % adds ~0.5-1.1 set/week at 15-20 sets (12_volume_algorithm_v1 §2.5); the v0 'INFERRED governor' comparison is retired. v1.1: one planned stairway for everyone (3 % then 5 %, λ-scaled: about 0.4-0.9 set a week for an L2 big muscle going 15 -> 22), moved only by the optional check-in; a recovery week between blocks, never a deload inside one (R2-PER-03/04, R2-VOL-03, R2-VOL-07). v1.2: approved and printed once, no check-ins (R3-VOL-02, R3-VOL-04); a recommended easy week between blocks (R3-PER-01).

science.claim: Strength/size maintained for up to 32 weeks with as little as 1 session/week and 1 set/exercise if relative load (intensity) is maintained; 1 strength session/week maintained strength, sprint and jump in pro soccer for 12 weeks, every second week did not.
science.citation: Spiering BA et al. J Strength Cond Res 2021; Ronnestad BR et al. J Strength Cond Res 2011; Cuthbert M et al. Sports Med 2021 (frequency can be distributed in-season).
science.maps_to: v1: in-season 2 days/week, low volume, keep intensity (COACH-ANSWER PER-08, UNI-10) now agrees with this evidence.

science.claim: Aerobic + strength does not blunt hypertrophy or maximal strength, but explosive strength gains are attenuated, mostly when both are in the same session.
science.citation: Schumann M et al. Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. Sports Med 2021.
science.maps_to: coach puts steady cardio on separate days (Wed/Sat) and short buy-outs at the END of sessions; CROSSFIT power months drop strength/resistance.

science.claim: Complex training improves sprint (5-20 m), COD and CMJ more than resistance training alone (low certainty); French contrast meta: large sprint and moderate jump effects, not max strength; >= 7-8 weeks and ~3 sessions/week optimise effects.
science.citation: Thapa RK et al. J Sports Sci 2024; Cormier P et al. J Strength Cond Res 2020; Zhao ZR et al. Front Physiol 2025.
science.maps_to: v1: contrast / French contrast and complexes for intermediate+ athletes in the off-season only (COACH-ANSWER ATH-12), so they sit in the off-season drive and hardest blocks (8.2.2), not pre-season.

science.claim: Common guideline: ~80-100 foot contacts/session beginner, 100-120 intermediate, 120-140 advanced (off-season). The PMC7873906 table is a study protocol (72 -> 126 contacts/session over 8 weeks in female basketball players, judged insufficient by its authors), not a ceiling; no source here supports a 200/400-contacts-per-session limit.
science.citation: NSCA Essentials (CSCS ch. 18) guideline as summarised by PT Pioneer; PMC7873906 (female basketball plyometric study, table 3).
science.maps_to: the coach's weekly contacts (32-324/week) sit well below per-session ceilings because plyos are spread over 2-4 short primers; low-amplitude reactive contacts can be much higher (squirrel jumps, rope).

science.claim: Acute:chronic workload ratio 0.8-1.3 described as a 'sweet spot'; spikes >1.5 associated with injury in team sports (the ratio is methodologically debated).
science.citation: Gabbett TJ. Br J Sports Med 2016 (summarised by Catapult / Vitruve).
science.maps_to: guardrail on week-to-week contact/sprint increases (<= ~10-15 %); the coach's 3/5/7 % is far inside it, his +41 % boxing wk3 jump is a phase change from 0 that should be preceded by base work.

science.claim: Max-effort (90-100 %) and dynamic-effort (Westside: roughly 50-60 % bar weight plus ~25 % band/chain tension, moved fast) days in the same week, rotating ME exercises every 1-3 weeks, with repeated-effort accessories.
science.citation: Westside Barbell 'Conjugate Method' (practitioner source); Zatsiorsky & Kraemer, Science and Practice of Strength Training.
science.maps_to: STRENGTH-8 is conjugate in structure ('conjugate style training') but the coach adds his own grammar (the work / accessory / nuance / survival; KD-HD alternation; plyo row labelled 'the work' on the speed day in the CONJUGATE draft). v1: 'I don't need it to be conjugate' (PER-01); band/chain tension out of scope (EQ-12).

science.claim: 13 studies: linear and daily undulating periodization gave similar muscle growth (d = -0.02, 95 % CI -0.25 to 0.21).
science.citation: Grgic J, Mikulic P, Podnar H, Pedisic Z. Effects of linear and daily undulating periodized resistance training programs on measures of muscle hypertrophy: a systematic review and meta-analysis. PeerJ 2017;5:e3695.
science.maps_to: Smooth weekly increases for hypertrophy (PER-10) are as good as fancier schemes; volume and effort matter more than the model. Supports the simple 12-week shape.

science.claim: 17 studies, 510 people: no difference between linear and undulating periodization for upper- or lower-body strength.
science.citation: Harries SK, Lubans DR, Callister R. Systematic review and meta-analysis of linear and undulating periodized resistance training programs on muscular strength. J Strength Cond Res 2015;29(4).
science.maps_to: The confirmed 2-week %-steps for strength (PER-09) are a valid choice, not the only one; the generator can keep his template.

science.claim: 18 studies: periodized plans improved 1RM more than non-periodized plans (ES 0.43); undulating programs and higher frequency/longer studies favoured larger gains.
science.citation: Williams TD, Tolusso DV, Fedewa MV, Esco MR. Comparison of periodized and non-periodized resistance training on maximal strength: a meta-analysis. Sports Med 2017;47(10).
science.maps_to: Planned variation between blocks (PER-02) and planned phases (PER-01) are worth having for strength; the shape itself is less important than having one.

science.claim: 10 weeks in Division I track and field athletes: no significant difference; block training produced similar strength with less volume (higher 'efficiency').
science.citation: Painter KB et al. Strength gains: block versus daily undulating periodization weight training among track and field athletes. Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2012;7(2).
science.maps_to: Athlete off-season blocks (VOL 1 -> 2 -> 3, PER-11) are a sound way to organise athletes.

science.topic: Early weeks of a new program
science.claim: Muscle damage is highest in week 1, lower by week 3 and minimal by week 10; protein synthesis tracks muscle growth only once damage has dropped (weeks 3 and 10, not week 1).
science.citation: Damas F et al. Resistance training-induced changes in integrated myofibrillar protein synthesis are related to hypertrophy only after attenuation of muscle damage. J Physiol 2016;594(18):5209-5222.
science.maps_to: Grounds his 2-4 'getting used to the movements' weeks: early volume mostly pays for repair, so the first steps are kept small. v1.1: there is no separate acclimation cap; the first-half stairway steps (3 %, λ-scaled) do this job (R2-PER-03, R2-PER-04).

science.claim: A first exposure to a new exercise protects against damage on later bouts; protection can last weeks to months and can be induced by submaximal or small doses.
science.citation: Nosaka K, Aoki MS. Repeated bout effect: research update and future perspective. Brazilian J Biomotricity 2011; McHugh MP. Recent advances in the understanding of the repeated bout effect. Scand J Med Sci Sports 2003.
science.maps_to: Supports a gentle acclimation. v1 also read it as support for an 8-week plan 'starting hard'; v1.1: that is retired (R2-PER-03 NOT RIGHT): every block, 8-week included, starts at the level start with small first steps, which is what the repeated-bout effect favours; after a layoff, use the 12-week acclimation (L1 weeks 1-4).

science.claim: Three 6-week training blocks separated by 3-week breaks gave similar muscle growth to 24 weeks of continuous training; growth rate after each break returned to the early-training rate.
science.citation: Ogasawara R, Yasuda T, Ishii N, Abe T. Comparison of muscle hypertrophy following 6-month of continuous and periodic strength training. Eur J Appl Physiol 2013.
science.maps_to: Maintenance/vacation blocks and repeated cycles do not cost long-term growth (PER-01); returning at the previous start after a maintenance block is safe.

science.claim: Meta-analysis of 103 studies: strength losses grow with time off; maximal strength was mostly unaffected for up to ~4 weeks (trivial effects), losses accelerate after that and are larger in people over 65 and in inactive people.
science.citation: Bosquet L et al. Effect of training cessation on muscular performance: a meta-analysis. Scand J Med Sci Sports 2013 (summary: Stronger by Science, 'Detraining').
science.maps_to: A 1-2-week vacation (PER-01) costs little; older clients keep the high end of maintenance (>= 70 %).

science.claim: Resistance training in an energy deficit (RCTs of 3+ weeks) blunted lean-mass gains; in the meta-regression a deficit of about 500 kcal/day predicted no lean-mass gain on average, while strength gains were not impaired.
science.citation: Murphy C, Koehler K. Energy deficiency impairs resistance training gains in lean mass but not strength: a meta-analysis and meta-regression. Scand J Med Sci Sports 2022.
science.maps_to: Fat-loss plans and the yearly Q1 cut hold volume near the level start (rate <= 3 %) and keep loads heavy; growth volume belongs to Q4 (PROPOSED). v1.1: the year's Q1 cut keeps sets at the starting level (R2-PER-01, approved); standalone fat-loss blocks use the standard stairway on the x0.8 start (12 v1.1); the v1 deficit cap is retired.

science.claim: Adults gain about 0.4-0.9 kg over the holiday season; the gain is small but is usually not lost later and is a large share of yearly weight gain.
science.citation: Yanovski JA et al. A prospective study of holiday weight gain. N Engl J Med 2000; Diaz-Zavala RG et al. Effect of the holiday season on weight gain: a narrative review. J Obes 2017.
science.maps_to: Automatic holiday maintenance (PER-01) keeps the habit going at low volume instead of stopping. v1.2: printed by default and, like every maintenance week, a recommendation the user can switch off (R3-PER-01).

science.claim: Eleven elite raw powerlifters (interviews) peaked volume 5.2 +/- 1.7 weeks and intensity 1.9 +/- 0.8 weeks before competition, cut volume by 58.9 +/- 8.4 % in the taper while keeping intensity, and trained last 3.7 +/- 1.6 days out.
science.citation: Pritchard HJ et al. Tapering practices of New Zealand's elite raw powerlifters. J Strength Cond Res 2016;30(7).
science.maps_to: Test week: reduce the rest of that week's volume and keep load (PER-07, PROPOSED dose); strength 'hardest' weeks peak intensity, not volume.

science.claim: Survey of 246 strength and physique athletes: deload every 5.6 +/- 2.3 weeks for 6.4 +/- 1.7 days, 79 % cut sets; a 1-week break in the middle of a 9-week program did not change growth and slightly reduced strength gains.
science.citation: Rogerson D, Bell L et al. Sports Med Open 2024; Coleman M et al. PeerJ 2024 (carried from 12_volume_algorithm_v1 §2.7).
science.maps_to: Most lifters deload more often than once per 12 weeks: the triggered deload (D6) will fire for many clients; the 'half the sets' dose (PER-05) matches practice. v1.1: no triggered deload any more (R2-VOL-07); the signals only offer 'cancel the block'; most lifters deload more often than every 12-13 weeks, so the 2 -> 11 stair, holds and the cancel option carry that load. v1.2: no check-in signals at all (R3-VOL-02); the easy first weeks, the person's own option to stop a block and the recommended easy week carry that load.

science.claim: After 16 weeks of training, 1/3 of the dose kept (and in young adults slightly grew) muscle size for 32 weeks; 1/9 kept size in the young; older adults needed more.
science.citation: Bickel CS, Cross JM, Bamman MM. Exercise dosing to retain resistance training adaptations in young and older adults. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2011 (carried from 12_volume_algorithm_v1 §2.4).
science.maps_to: His 50-70 % maintenance volume is well above the minimum; older clients >= 70 % (PER-01, PROPOSED floor).

science.claim: Classic periodization models rest on tradition more than evidence; responses vary widely between people, so plans should be responsive systems that adjust to the individual. A review of 42 periodization trials found mostly short studies of strength only, none longer than about 9 months, and individual responses ignored.
science.citation: Kiely J. Periodization paradigms in the 21st century: evidence-led or tradition-driven? Int J Sports Physiol Perform 2012;7(3):242-250; Afonso J et al. Is empirical research on periodization trustworthy? J Sports Sci Med 2017.
science.maps_to: Supports the week-by-week mode (GEN-05): the 12-week shape is a default. v1.1: the readiness-based rate is retired; the optional check-in (effort, completion, pain) moves the step, and with no check-in the planned stairway runs unchanged (R2-VOL-01, R2-VOL-03, R2-GEN-04). v1.2: the check-in and the week-by-week mode are retired (R3-VOL-02, R3-VOL-04); the plan is a printed default that the person or coach edits (R3-SES-02) - responsiveness without stored data.

science.claim: Practitioner models describe three ways to raise loads: straight-line, stepped (a jump then a hold) and wave-like (rise, then a lighter microcycle); the stepped method lets athletes master higher loads (Bompa).
science.citation: Bompa TO. Theory and Methodology of Training (stepped vs rectilinear vs wave loading), summarised by Stadion Books.
science.maps_to: Steps and waves for fight/competition prep (PER-10). No controlled study shows steps beat smooth increases for hypertrophy (see SCI_LP_DUP_HYP), so smooth stays the default for hypertrophy/general.

science.claim: After 20 weeks off, size returned to baseline but about 60 % of the strength gain remained (motor learning); older men regained their 1RM in under 8 weeks after 12 weeks off; regaining lost size and strength usually takes about half as long as the time off.
science.citation: Psilander N et al. Effects of training, detraining, and retraining on strength, hypertrophy, and myonuclear number in human skeletal muscle. J Appl Physiol 2019; Blocquiaux S et al. The effect of resistance training, detraining and retraining on muscle strength and power, myofibre size, satellite cells and myonuclei in older men. Exp Gerontol 2020; summary: Stronger by Science 'Detraining'.
science.maps_to: His layoff rule (PRG-05): after 6-12+ months off the body is treated as a beginner (L1 volume) while skills come back fast (exercise level kept); ex-pros stay at L1 only briefly. The 12-week acclimation (4 weeks for returning clients) fits.

science.claim: Resistance-trained men kept their leg-press strength and lean mass after 2 weeks of detraining.
science.citation: Hwang PS et al. Resistance training-induced elevations in muscular strength in trained men are maintained after 2 weeks of detraining and not differentially affected by whey protein supplementation. J Strength Cond Res 2017.
science.maps_to: A 1-2-week vacation (PER-01) inside a maintenance block costs little: ~50 % with what is available, or full rest, then return at the previous start (D5, PROPOSED).

science.claim: Common power guidance: multiple-effort power work at 75-85 % 1RM for 3-5 reps per set, single-effort at 80-90 % for 1-2 reps, 3-5 sets with 2-5 min rest; pulling derivatives (no catch) allow heavier loads and similar or greater force and velocity than catch variants.
science.citation: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, power load assignment (summary); Suchomel TJ, Comfort P, Lake JP. Enhancing the force-velocity profile of athletes using weightlifting derivatives. Strength Cond J 2017.
science.maps_to: Science check he asked for in PER-09: his 4 x 6 @ 80-85 % and 4 x 4 @ 90 % sit close to this guidance; 4 x 8 @ 75 % is more reps per set than usual for full catch lifts (technique fades late in long sets). Fine for DB/KB and hang-pull variants; for full lifts a 3-5-rep option is PROPOSED (round-2 question). v1.1: approved (R2-ATH-05): full lifts 3-5 reps per set; DB/KB and pull variants keep 4 x 8.

science.claim: Meta-analysis (endurance athletes incl. swimmers): the best taper lasts about 8-14 days with a 41-60 % volume cut and intensity and frequency kept. A 2024 randomized trial in competitive swimmers: a 2-week progressive taper (-30 % then -50 % volume, sprint intensity kept) improved 50 m front-crawl time by 3.5 % (control 1.4 %) and lowered total mood disturbance by 14 %.
science.citation: Bosquet L et al. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2007; Aouani H, Amara S, Rebai H, Barbosa TM, van den Tillaar R. Optimizing performance and mood state in competitive swimmers through tapering strategies. Front Psychol 2024;15:1307675.
science.maps_to: Swimmers' championship meets get a 2-week dryland taper lined up with the pool taper (PROPOSED, 14.3 #6); his 1-2-week pre-season taper (R2-PER-06) sits inside the evidence. v1.2: approved (COACH-R3 R3-ATH-01): 2 weeks with the swim taper before the main championship meet, 1 week or none before smaller meets.

science.claim: HYROX = eight 1-km runs, each followed by a station (SkiErg 1000 m, sled push 50 m, sled pull 50 m, burpee broad jumps 80 m, row 1000 m, farmers carry 200 m, sandbag lunges 100 m, wall balls 100); performance depends on aerobic capacity (the foundation), anaerobic power, local muscular endurance and maximal strength; sport-specific research is still limited.
science.citation: Davids CJ. A performance analysis of HYROX: a review of the physiologic, mechanical, and technical demands. Strength Cond J 2026;48(1):88-100.
science.maps_to: Gen-pop 'stay athletic and active' HYROX overlay: aerobic 3-4 sessions, station circuits as density work, a resistance stairway for legs, pulling and carries; 1-week taper before a race (PROPOSED). v1.2: HYROX plan approved (COACH-R3 R3-ATH-03): 2 strength + 2 hybrid days, 4 cardio sessions, 2 station circuits as finishers that never count as muscle sets, wall balls <= 20 lb, 40-rep / AMRAP only in the circuits; race taper = the R3-ATH-05 event peak.

science.claim: 24.3 million Americans played pickleball in 2025 (about 4.2 million in 2020); +171.8 % from 2022 to 2025, the fastest-growing sport in the US; strong engagement among adults 25-44 and players 65+.
science.citation: Sports & Fitness Industry Association (SFIA). U.S. Pickleball Participation (2025 data).
science.maps_to: Supports a gen-pop 'stay athletic and active' path with pickleball (coach request) and the 60+ rules for many players (R2-ATH-08). v1.2: racket 50+ rules and 60+ defaults approved (COACH-R3 R3-ATH-02).

science.claim: In 70 adults aged 18-69 of mixed training experience, a 5RM predicted the 1RM best (R2 0.993 bench press, 0.974 leg press), better than 10RM or 20RM tests.
science.citation: Reynolds JM, Gordon TJ, Robergs RA. Prediction of one repetition maximum strength from multiple repetition maximum testing and anthropometry. J Strength Cond Res 2006;20(3):584-592.
science.maps_to: Supports his rule that people starting from zero test a 5RM (or 3RM) and estimate the max instead of testing a 1RM (R2-PER-07).

open_questions.question: The week-by-week mode needed weekly check-ins and a saved history. Without them, is it fine to drop it and serve 'keep me in line' with the year plan or one block after another?
open_questions.proposal: Yes: drop week-by-week; the year plan or the next block covers it.

open_questions.question: Nothing is saved, so to start the next block one step up the plan has to ask. OK to add one intake question: 'Did you just finish a block?'
open_questions.proposal: Yes, with how many in a row (0 by default; 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.12): each completed block -> start x1.05, cap +1; none -> the level start.

open_questions.question: If someone switches off a recommended easy week in the year plan, should the next block start a week earlier (and the spare week go to the December holidays)?
Athletes: one printed plan from the season dates covering the off-season blocks and the pre-season to the first game, then they build the in-season plan in the app?

The year's Q1 cut keeps the sets at the starting level (your round-2 answer), while round 3 says the stairway always climbs on the groups that are trained. OK that in Q1 the climb comes from cardio, density, load and effort instead of sets?
open_questions.proposal: Yes: keep the Q1 sets flat; every week still feels harder (the 2 -> 11 stair).

open_questions.question: Some lines cannot reach their ceiling with the approved steps (an 8-week beginner big muscle ends at 13 of 14; an intermediate's shoulders 12 -> 18 of 22 in 12 weeks). Should the ceiling stay a maximum (the plan stops below it), or should the steps grow above about 5 % so every line lands exactly on it?
open_questions.proposal: Keep the ceiling as a maximum; never plan steps above about 5 %.

changes.change: Plan lengths rebuilt. The v0 fixed shapes (8 weeks = 7 loading + deload/test; 12 weeks = 6 + week-7 mid deload + 5; 6 weeks = first half of the 12) are retired. v1 modes: 4-6-week maintenance/transition at about 50-70 % volume (vacation, travel, season change, moving); 8 weeks = 4 adapting + 4 driving hard, starting hard; 12 weeks (preferred) = 2-4 acclimation + 4-6 driving hard (not to the top) + hardest last weeks; repeated 12-week cycles start one level higher ('start at a 2 and end at an 11'); open-ended week-by-week mode; yearly mode with quarter themes and automatic holiday maintenance.

Deloads: the v0 fixed deload/test weeks (week 8 of 8, week 7 of 12, week 6 of 6) are retired with the shapes he rejected. Deload dose confirmed: about half the sets, same exercises, lighter load or 3+ RIR, no buy-out or finisher. Placement is PROPOSED and aligned with 12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.12: triggered by the logs, week 1 of the next cycle, or replaced by a maintenance block.

Weekly progression = 3, 5 or 7 % of a muscle's weekly sets, chosen by the PERSON's state (fatigue, life, response), coach-adjustable; 10 %/week is too much (hard ceiling). The v0 size tiers (big 3 % / medium 5 % / small 7 %), the focus 'one tier up' rule and the v0 worked example are retired.
Rounding: bank the fraction every week and add a whole set when the bank reaches 1; the tool computes the percentages, not the client.

Where a new set goes: 3-4 exercises per muscle per day; add to the first exercise in session order, then the next (2/2/2 -> 3/2/2 -> 3/3/2 -> 3/3/3 -> 4/3/3); small muscles at the end of a session get extra volume as a bonus exercise.

Smooth weekly increases for hypertrophy and general clients; 2-week steps and waves for fight or competition prep. The v0 'STEP mode default for strength/athlete/hybrid' is retired; the confirmed strength %-template is the competition-style step pattern for main lifts.

Strength %-template confirmed (Olympic lifts 75 -> 80 -> 85 -> 90 % with 4x8 -> 4x6 -> 4x6 -> 4x4; main lift 80/80/85/85/90/90 % with RPE 7 -> 10) and placed inside the v1 12-week shape. He added 'I just want to make sure it's correct', so a science check is attached: the main-lift loads sit within about 1-4 percentage points of the RPE chart; the Olympic 4 x 8 @ 75 % is above common power guidance (3-5 reps per set at 75-85 %) for full catch lifts and is flagged for round 2.

Set counting: helpers 0.25 (not 0.5); dips 0.5 triceps / 0.5 chest; a 10/10 unilateral set = 1 set; athletic patterns (plyos, ballistics, throws, Olympic lifts, sprints) never count toward muscle volume.

Blocks are 4-6 weeks; exercises stay fixed inside a block; the next block changes 1-2 small variables (grip, stance, implement, range of motion, rep range). A/B lead-lift weeks are an option for clients who want variety, not a default.

The second exposure of a slot in a week is a different exercise from the same category, and axial spinal loading happens once a week (squat one day; leg press or belt squat the other; deadlifts load the spine too).
A slot moves up a level at the end of a block if it felt '8 - That was perfect' or easier with no pain. Exercise levels are still theoretical; do not over-rely on them.
Tests: the client or coach ticks what to test at the start of a block (strength, cardio, speed, ...) or 'No need for testing'; the plan schedules the test at the end of the block and reminds them.

Athlete seasons confirmed: off-season most volume (strength + plyos); pre-season more speed/power, less volume; in-season 2 days/week, low volume (sprints for speed athletes, strength maintenance or jumps for others; bilateral work minimal); post-season recovery and general work.
VOL 1 / VOL 2 / VOL 3 (compound 12-15 / 8-12 / 6-8 reps) = one rep phase per off-season block for every athlete.
Off-season STARTING / MID / ADVANCED: back-to-back blocks or athlete levels, 'depends on whatever is needed' (decision rule PROPOSED).

Week-to-week adjustment from logged EFFORT and HOW IT FELT confirmed; the person-level readiness rate of 12_volume_algorithm_v1 replaces the v0 per-muscle autoregulation table. The GEN-03 'they should track it themselves' conflict is handled by a static vs adaptive output mode (PROPOSED).

Effort: RIR is the model (1-3 RIR at all times, RPE explained alongside); 'MAX' = technical failure only on small-muscle or bodyweight work; never to failure on heavy compounds. A ramp inside the 1-3 RIR band across the phases is PROPOSED.
Rest: hypertrophy 1-2 min (up to 3), strength 3-6 min, athletic as prescribed.

Methods: MYO sets only on the last machine/isolation exercise; supersets are a fatigue/density tool (short time, advanced clients needing more stimulus, off-season VO2/mitochondrial work, beginners who do not fatigue); contrast / French contrast and complexes for intermediate+ athletes in the off-season only (heavy lift about 78-85 %).

No bands and no variable resistance (bands, chains, weight releasers, reverse-banded assistance) in any generator rule; banded/chained cells stay only as OBSERVED evidence. Speed lifts use straight weight ('FAST RPE6 or about 60-70%').

Plyo 'zones' are not zones: they are method stages, receive & pause -> receive then create -> repeated receive/create (name pending). Programs start more ballistic and become more plyometric; the plyo:ballistic ratio follows the sport's ground-contact time; unilateral plyos are harder than bilateral. Davidson zones (rotation biases) do not apply to plyos.

Olympic lifts for everyone in athletic training (beginners: DB/KB snatches, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls/cleans; intermediate+: full lifts; youth may lift from the floor). Full lifts are named 'Squat Snatch', 'Squat Clean', 'Squat Clean & Jerk'; push press is easier, push jerk intermediate/advanced.
Aerobic sessions per week: 3 general/fat loss, 2 athletes in-season, 4 aesthetics/bodybuilders, plus long walks after workouts; any erg works, tracked by calories, time or distance.
Core first by default (warm-up), movable by the user; about 2 core exercises; calves 3 sets every leg day; rear delts get their own sets.

Reps: small muscles 12-30, big muscles 5-15; 40-rep sets only as a CrossFit/AMRAP option (the FAT BURN 40-rep isolation ladder is not a generator default); client preference moves the reps on big compounds only; '12/10/8 -20' = pyramid 12 (mid) / 10 (heavier) / 8 (heaviest) then a light set of 20; '10/10' = per side.
Boxers/strikers: reduce (do not cut) pressing and arm volume in weeks of high punching volume.
No medball work for aesthetics/bodybuilding clients except in the warm-up; medballs never over 20 lb; throws have no levels.

Older clients: few plyos unless they ask; extra volume on constrained machines; never overhead squat, snatch, low-bar squat or depth jumps. No sex-based rules (age, foundation, goal, injuries decide).

Bilateral:unilateral share spans 90/10 to 10/90 and moves across blocks: bodybuilders/powerlifters about 50/50 at the start (contra/ipsi health work in the first 2-4 weeks) -> 80/20-90/10; field/change-of-direction athletes 80-90 % unilateral; in-season minimal bilateral; pain adjusts it.
Pairing: same pattern (squat + lunge) for high-level/aesthetics clients, cross pattern for bootcamp; hip dominant + push and knee dominant + pull for full-body and bootcamp days.

Session size: resistance-only 5-7 exercises; field athletes off-season up to 10-12 (2 core + 2-4 plyo/ballistic + 2-3 Olympic/power + 3-4 resistance); about 1.5 h (max 2 h) for athletes, bodybuilders and powerlifters, 45-60 min for general/weight loss.
Bootcamp: timed circuits 3-5 rounds x 30-50 s, 5-7 stations, 35-45 min, 3-6 sessions a week; FAT BURN circuits are finishers after lifting.
Levels L1/L2/L3 (novice = newby: under ~6-12 months; intermediate: consistent over a year; 6-12+ months off -> body treated as beginner, skills return fast; ex-pros at L1 only briefly).
CrossFit dose tables: FULL TIME = competitor, HALF TIME = class member. Half-marathon plan (Chris Hinshaw) used as-is.
'JUSTICE LEAGUE' was a marketing name: the program is the weekend-warrior athletic program (non-competitive athletic adults and youth). Renamed everywhere outside verbatim cell quotes.

Davidson zones are rotation biases (vertical = external-rotation bias; horizontal = internal-rotation bias, compressive); level reads from load position (front-loaded foundational, on the body intermediate, behind/overhead advanced; machines easier).
'camporini deadlift' and 'strap rotating in/out' are dropped from the generator (they remain as OBSERVED cell quotes).

pending.item: Yearly mode: quarter themes as transcribed (Q1 hard work + more cardio, cutting toward summer; Q2 lose fat / get in shape for summer, a mix of building some muscle and keeping fat down; Q3 maintain; Q4 build muscle in winter; last 2 weeks of December automatic maintenance). His Q1/Q2 wording is ambiguous; calendar anchor (hemisphere, personal dates, other holidays) not decided.
Deload placement inside the 12- and 8-week shapes: none planned; triggered by the logs, or week 1 of the next cycle (12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.12).

12-week week split (acclimation weeks 1-3, L1 1-4, L3 1-2; drive to week 9, L3 to week 8; hardest weeks 10-12, L3 9-12, so every level drives for 4-6 weeks as he said), acclimation rate <= 3 %, 8-week start x 1.10 and rate <= 5 % in weeks 1-4.
Maintenance factors by reason (50 % vacation/limited kit, 60 % travel/moving/season change, 70 % planned maintenance; older adults >= 70 %), base = mean of the last 4 loading weeks.
Repeated cycles: next start = previous start x 1.05, cap +1 (max 25 non-priority / 30 priority); same start after holds, pain or a maintenance block.
Week-by-week mode: block boundary every 4-6 weeks; deload on triggers or after 12 loading weeks at the latest; requires logs (adaptive output).
RIR ramp inside his 1-3 RIR band: acclimation 2-3, drive 1-2, hardest 1; maintenance 2-3; deload 3+.
Strength %-template placement: acclimation weeks at ~70-75 % (RPE 6-7), drive = STRENGTH-12 weeks 1-6, hardest = STRENGTH-12 weeks 10-12 doses (~90/92/95 %).
Test catalogue, test week (test day replaces the top sets; rest of that week -30-50 %), reminder schedule (block start, 7 days and 1 day before).
In-season dose: 2 sessions/week; resistance x0.4-0.5 lower / x0.3-0.4 upper; 1-2 main lifts at 3-6 reps, RIR 2-3; >= 80-90 % unilateral.
Pre-season = the 'season change' 4-6-week block at maintenance-level resistance volume with speed/power emphasis; 1-2-week taper before the opener.
PRG-04 decision rule: off-season >= 16 weeks and L1-L2 -> STARTING, MID, ADVANCED as consecutive blocks; shorter off-season or L3 -> pick the template by level.
Fat loss / cut quarter: rate <= 3 % while in a calorie deficit; Q1 holds the level start instead of stepping up.
Fight prep: 2-week steps and waves; if a fight date is set, the last 1-2 weeks taper (the observed BOXING build-up ends at a week-8 peak). v0 question 14 is still unanswered.
Name and week split of the plyo method stages: 'Receive-Create stages' RC1 (weeks 1-2), RC2 (weeks 3-5), RC3 (week 6+).

Variety preference as an intake input that switches on A/B lead-lift weeks.

Fat-loss skeleton curves: rate capped at 3 % in a calorie deficit for every week, so the reference curves climb 10 -> 13 (L1), 15 -> 20 (L2), 20 -> 25 (L3) over 12 weeks.
Complexes inside a fight camp (ATH-12 says off-season only; the BOXING build-up uses them from week 3).

headline_rules_v0_observed: R1 Quality x level x time: a plan is a grid of qualities (resistance/hypertrophy, strength, power, aerobic, WODs/conditioning, athletic patterns, test) with a level per period; a dose table converts level -> sets x reps (CROSSFIT A10:M17 + A19:U25). OBSERVED.

R2 Default sequence inside any block that ends in a peak: hypertrophy/base -> strength -> power -> test/realization (CROSSFIT blocks; BOXING base -> conversion; BASEBALL off -> pre -> in). OBSERVED (the BASEBALL blocks are labelled only 'BLOCK 1/2/3': their season reading is INFERRED).

R3 Plan shapes: 8 weeks = 7 loading + deload/test week 8 (exceptions: BOXING ends at a peak, HYBRID-8 has no deload, CROSSFIT class week 8 = 1RM test only); 12 weeks = 6 loading + 'MID DELOAD' week 7 + 5 loading weeks (AESTHETICS-12: new menu + intensifiers; STRENGTH-12: same A/B menu restarting at the wk3-4 dose), peak week 12. OBSERVED. 6 weeks = first half of the 12-week shape. INFERRED.

R4 Volume moves in whole-set steps (+1 set per exercise every 2-3 weeks) inside rep waves; the long-run average of those steps is 4-6 %/week in the 12-week products and FAT BURN (the 8-week products that start at 2 sets run 10-17 %/week), which is read as the coach's stated 3/5/7 %. OBSERVED numbers, INFERRED reconciliation.

R5 Compound reps fall while isolation reps rise or go to 'MAX' (BASEBALL legend 'COMPOUND' vs 'SMALLER ISOLATIONS' VOL 1-3; FAT BURN leg ext/curl slot 15 -> 20 -> 40 -> 40). Big muscles progress by load/sets, small muscles by reps/effort. OBSERVED (exception: PPL side raises/rear flies/upright rows follow the compound ladder 3x15 -> 4x8).

R6 Effort words are written per row in the conjugate tabs and follow the exercise role: max-effort AND dynamic-effort lifts '1RIR', second compound 4x6 '2RIR', upper/unilateral accessory 4x8-10 'MAX', 2-3 x '8/8' finisher 'ALL', plyo 'EASY' (Mon/Wed these are the 1st-4th rows; on Thursday the plyo row comes first, so pull-ups = 3rd row '2RIR' and lunges = 4th row 'MAX'); strength waves RPE 7 -> 9/10 (STRENGTH-12); hypertrophy '1-2 RIR' (AESTHETICS-8 only); never grind main lifts to failure. OBSERVED words; the 'unilateral = MAX / isolation = ALL' class mapping is INFERRED (STRENGTH-8 'MAX' rows are pull-ups, DB bench and lunges; its 'ALL' rows are lunges and curls).

R7 Deload = same template at 3 sets per main exercise (BASEBALL 3 x 8; AESTHETICS-12 3 x '8/8/8-12'; STRENGTH-12 3 x 4 @ RPE 7), intensifiers/conditioning/Olympic lifts removed, athletic Part A 1-2 sets; volume -25 to -50 %. OBSERVED; one unified '3 x 8 @ RPE ~7' default is INFERRED.

R8 Gym clients progress by ADDING volume with level (NOVICE -> NEWBY -> INTERMEDIATE: 76 -> 90 -> 102 sets); athletes progress by CUTTING volume and raising intensity/specificity (STARTING -> MID -> ADVANCED: 89 -> 72 -> 59 component sets, ~61 -> ~54 -> ~44 written line sets; resistance flat 44 -> 44 before falling to 24; heaviest hinge 3x6 'Heavy Snatch grip DL' -> 3x1 'DEADLIFTS (1RIR)'). OBSERVED cells, counts computed.

R9 Athletes: off-season = build (new menus, 12/10/8/8, base then conversion), pre-season = intensify/potentiate (contrast, complexes, 8/6/4/4, Oly 75 -> 90 %, sets 4 -> 5, deload before opener), in-season = maintain (Part C/D frozen at 4 x 8-10, Part A 1-3 and core 2-4 sets, no Oly, no Part C compound < 8 reps, 2 alternating familiar menus, upper supersets and banded lifts kept). OBSERVED (block-to-season mapping INFERRED).

R10 Athletic work stays in every training phase: plyos and throws in off-, pre- and in-season (BASEBALL ~200 contacts and ~180 throws/week); only the zone/amplitude and the slot quality change. Exceptions: the boxer's 2 base weeks (throws only, zero plyos), the BASEBALL Block 1 'wk 8' recovery week (no plyos or throws) and deloads (Part A 1-2 sets). OBSERVED (BASEBALL season labels INFERRED).

R11 Variation changes ONE variable at a time inside a fixed pattern slot (A/B weeks, one lunge variable per week, 2-week upgrades); the slot skeleton is held inside a phase and changes at phase boundaries (BOXING wk3 new menu; AESTHETICS-12 wk8-9 drops the Mon/Thu 'TRICEP EXT.' rows and rebuilds Friday around unilateral/isolation work). OBSERVED.

R12 Intensification methods (supersets, MYO, max-rep finishers, complexes, French contrast, bands/chains) are concentrated in the last phase of hypertrophy plans and in the conversion/pre-season phases of athletic plans; never in deload weeks (exceptions: MYO preset on leg extensions in BYOP ATHLETIC week 1; contrast pairs in athletic STARTING; BASEBALL upper-body 'Superset - same reps'/'Superset - max reps' pairs, 'heavy Max reps' sets and banded lifts in all three blocks incl. Block 1 week 1 and in-season Block 3 - only the '5 of each' complexes and 'myo set' / 'myo sets' are Block-2-only). OBSERVED.

R13 Conditioning progresses by unlocking zones (C -> C+B -> C+B+A -> lactate clearance) and by density (rounds x seconds), not by making one session longer; steady cardio lives on separate days (Wed/Sat). OBSERVED.

testing.rule: Tests are ticked at the start of a block (strength, cardio, speed and agility, jumps, body weight) or 'No need for testing' (default). Test before the block (or in week 1) and at the end; never during the block.
testing.coach_words: R2-PER-07: 'You should be able to test before and then test at the end.' ... 'they should not test during the weeks, during the block.' ... 'you should not go from not training to a one-rep max test.' ... 'They should try to test at 80%, 90%, but not at 100%.'
testing.safety: 'Starting from zero' = no completed training block (new, untrained, or back after 6+ months off): strength by a 5RM (or 3RM) with an estimated 1RM; cardio and speed at 80-90 % effort (e.g. a 1-mile at a hard but controlled pace, an erg piece at a fixed effort, sprints at 80-90 %); never a 1RM, a max-effort mile or an all-out sprint. After a completed block: intermediate and advanced may take a 3RM or work up to a 1RM at the END of a block. Older adults (60+): submax tests only (PROPOSED).

science_grounding.his_rule: 'The first 2 to 4 weeks are going to be just you getting used to the movements' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: Damas 2016: hypertrophy signal mostly after ~3 weeks, once damage drops; repeated bout effect: early exposures protect
science_grounding.verdict: Supported. v1.1: these are the first small steps of the stairway (3 %, λ-scaled) at 3 RIR.

science_grounding.shape: 12-week stairway: small steps to halfway, bigger after, last 4 weeks hardest
science_grounding.his_rule: 'steps up a stairway ... that goes for every plan' (R2-PER-03); 'the last 4 weeks are going to be brutal' (R2-PER-04)
science_grounding.evidence: RP/Enes/Pelland: more weekly sets -> more growth with diminishing returns; Grgic 2017, Harries 2015, Moesgaard 2022: the periodization model matters little when volume is equal; Williams 2017: planned plans beat unplanned for strength
science_grounding.verdict: Supported: a gradual volume ramp to a hard finish, then recovery, is the RP mesocycle logic; equal-volume models give similar growth (Grgic 2017), so the value is in the gradual ramp and the planned recovery.

science_grounding.shape: No deload inside a block; a recommended easy week between blocks
science_grounding.his_rule: 'It should never be thrown in the middle of a block' (R2-VOL-07)
science_grounding.evidence: Rogerson 2024: deload every ~5.6 weeks in practice; Bell 2023: planned or autoregulated both acceptable; Coleman 2024: a 1-week break mid-program did not change growth
science_grounding.verdict: Plausible: Coleman 2024 found a mid-program week off did not help growth; practitioners deload every ~5-6 weeks (Rogerson 2024), so his blocks rely on the 2 -> 11 stair (easy first weeks), the person's own option to stop a block and the recommended easy week between blocks, which matches the Bell 2023 placement option (R3-PER-01).

science_grounding.his_rule: R2-PER-03 (NOT RIGHT on 4 + 4 and 'start hard'): the same stairway as every plan
science_grounding.evidence: Scarpelli 2022 / Barsuhn 2024 (in 12_vol): trained people do well starting from their previous volume; repeated bout effect
science_grounding.verdict: Supported: the same gradual ramp; the repeated bout effect and Damas 2016 favour small early steps.

science_grounding.his_rule: 'a lower-volume maintenance volume ... 70 % ... 50 %. This allows them to recover and not push too hard' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: Bickel 2011 (1/3 of the dose keeps size in the young), Spiering 2021, Bosquet 2013 (strength stable ~4 weeks off), Ogasawara 2013 (breaks do not cost long-term growth)
science_grounding.verdict: Well supported; older adults stay >= 70 %; even a beginner's 6-9 sets are above the research minimum for keeping size (Bickel 2011).

science_grounding.his_rule: 'start at a 2 and end at an 11' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: Scarpelli 2022 (progressing from the person's own previous volume worked); Pelland 2026 (each extra step of growth costs more sets); Ogasawara 2013
science_grounding.verdict: Supported with a ceiling: advanced clients climb by load, intensifiers and a rotating priority muscle, not only sets (approved, COACH-R2 R2-PER-05).

science_grounding.his_rule: 'Just keep me in line ... and then it does it by itself' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: Kiely 2012 (responsive planning), Hickmott 2022 (autoregulation as good as % plans; in 12_vol)
science_grounding.verdict: Retired: without check-ins and stored data it cannot respond week to week (R3-VOL-02, R3-GEN-01); responsiveness now comes from the person or coach editing the printed plan (R3-SES-02).

science_grounding.his_rule: R2-PER-01/02 (approved for gen-pop 'stay in shape'; user-tunable)
science_grounding.evidence: No controlled trials of annual plans for general clients (Afonso 2017: no periodization trial longer than ~9 months); Issurin/Kiely frameworks; Murphy & Koehler 2022 (cut phases protect muscle, not grow it); Yanovski 2000 / Diaz-Zavala 2017 (holiday gain)
science_grounding.verdict: Coaching choice with sensible support; approved by the coach for gen pop.

science_grounding.evidence: Bompa step/wave loading (practitioner); taper evidence (Bosquet 2007, Pritchard 2016); no hypertrophy advantage for any model (Grgic 2017)
science_grounding.verdict: Supported as a peaking tool; smooth stays the default elsewhere.

science_grounding.shape: Returning after a layoff (6-12+ months off) and ex-pros
science_grounding.his_rule: body treated as a beginner, skills come back fast; ex-pros at Level 1 only briefly (PRG-05)
science_grounding.evidence: Psilander 2019, Blocquiaux 2020: strength and skill persist longer than size; regaining takes about half the time off
science_grounding.verdict: Supported: L1 volume with a 4-week acclimation, exercise level kept, level-up check after the first block (PROPOSED).

science_grounding.his_rule: 'a vacation 1-week or vacation 2-week kind of thing' (PER-01)
science_grounding.evidence: Hwang 2017: strength and lean mass kept after 2 weeks off; Bosquet 2013: maximal strength mostly kept up to ~4 weeks
science_grounding.verdict: Supported: ~50 % with what is available, or full rest; return at the previous start.

science_grounding.shape: Strength %-template and Olympic ramp (PER-09: 'I just want to make sure it's correct')
science_grounding.evidence: RTS RPE chart (section 5.3); NSCA power guidance (75-85 % for 3-5 reps); Suchomel 2017 (pull variants allow heavier loads); Harries 2015 (linear steps as good as undulating for strength)
science_grounding.verdict: Main lift: consistent (loads within about 1-4 points of the chart). Olympic 4 x 8 @ 75 %: high for full catch lifts; fine for DB/KB and pull variants; flagged (14.2). v1.1: full squat cleans/snatches use 3-5 reps per set (R2-ATH-05); weight by RPE and speed unless a tested max (R2-GEN-06).

science_grounding.evidence: Issurin 2010: accumulation 2-6 weeks -> transmutation 2-4 -> realization; strength residuals ~30 +/- 5 days, explosive ~5 +/- 3 days; Painter 2012
science_grounding.verdict: Supported; keep plyos/sprints in every phase because explosive residuals are short.

science_grounding.shape: Testing before and after, submax from zero
science_grounding.his_rule: R2-PER-07: test before and at the end, never mid-block; 5RM/3RM or 80-90 % from zero
science_grounding.evidence: Reynolds 2006: a 5RM predicted the 1RM best (R2 0.99 bench, 0.97 leg press) in adults of mixed experience aged 18-69
science_grounding.verdict: Supported: safe baselines lose little accuracy.

science_grounding.evidence: Bosquet 2007 (taper 8-14 days, volume -41-60 %, intensity kept); Vachon 2020 (team sports); Ronnestad 2011 / Spiering 2021 (maintenance with low volume when intensity is kept)

science_grounding.his_rule: COACH-R3 R3-ATH-01 (approved: 2 weeks lined up with the swim taper; 1 week or none before smaller meets)
science_grounding.evidence: Bosquet 2007; Aouani 2024 (2-week progressive taper, +3.5 % 50 m time)

science_grounding.his_rule: COACH-R3 R3-ATH-05 (approved: hardest weeks end 1 week before, then 1 easy week at about half the sets)
science_grounding.evidence: Bosquet 2007 (best taper 8-14 days, volume -41-60 %, intensity kept)
science_grounding.verdict: Supported at the short end of the evidence (1 week) for recreational events.

planned_steps_pct.lambda: if start x growth > cap, every step of that muscle is multiplied by one factor λ < 1 so the planned peak lands on the cap in week N (12-week big muscles: L1 0.76, L2 0.87, L3 0.50; 8-week: L1 1, L2 1, L3 0.78)
planned_steps_pct.older_60_plus_v1_2: RETIRED in v1.2: the v1.1 PROPOSED 60+ <= 3 % cap (12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.4, §3.7.4; COACH-R3 R3-VOL-04 - every trained group reaches its ceiling in the last week); 60+ are protected by the R3-ATH-02 defaults and constrained machines (EQ-03)

stairway.halves: first half = weeks 2..ceil(N/2); second half = weeks ceil(N/2)+1..N (week 1 has no step). 12 weeks: 3 % in weeks 2-6, 5 % in weeks 7-12; 8 weeks: 3 % in weeks 2-4, 5 % in weeks 5-8.
stairway.person_total_ceiling: the person's total weekly sets rise by less than 10 % a week; when several muscles would release a set in the same week, the smallest banks wait one week (release staggering, PROPOSED; COACH-ANSWER UNI-05)
stairway.bank_rule: the bank is the planned target minus the current sets (T - current; the same as banking step x current sets each week); place one whole set each time it reaches 1 (12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.8): usually one set a week, two only when a λ-anchored final week needs it (e.g. the 11-week year Q4 block, week 50: 22 -> 24; release staggering spreads such jumps across muscles); at the cap the bank is cleared and the week climbs by load, reps, RIR or intensifiers (COACH-ANSWER VOL-06, VOL-07, VOL-15)
stairway.dial_rule: every week at least one dial moves up: a set is released, or the main lifts go heavier at the same RIR (or +1-2 reps), or the RIR target steps down per the phase table; the last week is the block's highest volume and load (PROPOSED, from R2-PER-04/05)
stairway.checkin_rule: RETIRED in v1.2: there are no check-ins (R3-VOL-02, R3-VOL-04); the plan prints the planned step of every week
stairway.stair_level: display only: level(w) = 2 + 9 x A(w) / A(N), where A adds 1 for each first-half step and 5/3 for each second-half step (the same weights as the steps); 12 weeks: 2, 2.6, 3.2, 3.8, 4.4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11; 8 weeks: 2, 2.9, 3.9, 4.8, 6.3, 7.9, 9.4, 11 (PROPOSED; the same display as 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.7.2)

phases.other_N: ACCLIMATION = the first ~quarter (at least week 1), HARDEST = the last third (rounded up), DRIVE in between (e.g. 11-week year block: ACCLIMATION 1-3, DRIVE 4-7, HARDEST 8-11)

exercise_blocks.rule: exercises fixed inside each; 1-2 one-detail changes at the boundary (PER-02, R2-LIB-01)

stairway.tags: COACH-R2 R2-PER-03, R2-PER-04, R2-PER-05 (shape); COACH-R3 R3-VOL-04 (steps, halves, λ peak on the cap in the last week and the RIR drift approved); 8-week phase weeks, dial rule and stair-level display PROPOSED; the set math is owned by 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.7

block_flow.diagram:
TRAINING BLOCK (a stairway: week 1 feels like a '2' ... last week feels like an '11'), printed whole before it starts
  baseline test before the block or in week 1 (if ticked; submax if no completed block)
  weeks run in order; NO deload or maintenance week inside; no check-ins - the person or coach may lighten a day
  themselves (switch off the athletic or core block, remove a set or an exercise) without changing the stairway
  |
  +-- block COMPLETED -> end test in the last week (if ticked) -> THE BLOCK ENDS (the plan ends here)
  |      printed recommendation (not mandatory): an EASY WEEK (about half the sets of the hardest week,
  |      same exercises, 3+ RIR) as an extra week before the next block
  |      the user goes back into the app and builds what they want next:
  |        - the next block one step up ('I just finished a block' -> start x1.05, cap +1)
  |        - a maintenance phase (choose its length)
  |        - a different plan
  |
  +-- the person or coach STOPS the block (their call; a holiday marked after the start also ends it)
         -> MAINTENANCE PHASE (choose the number of weeks)
         -> when it ends, the plan ends; the user builds the next plan in the app
         -> usually a whole new block from week 1 at the SAME start as the stopped block (no easy week: maintenance was the recovery)
after_a_block: the block ends (the plan ends here)
recommended, not mandatory: an easy week at about half the sets of the hardest week (an extra week)
the user builds the next block one step up ('I just finished a block'), a maintenance phase or another plan in the app
after_maintenance: the user builds what comes next in the app: keep maintaining, change the plan or start a training block (his R2-PER-06 options)
block_flow.tags: COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07, R2-PER-06; COACH-R3 R3-PER-01 (approved + note), R3-VOL-02, R3-GEN-01; intake question PROPOSED

event_peak_genpop.rule: optional event date for gen pop (a first HYROX race, a pickleball tournament, a 10K): the hardest weeks end 1 week before, then 1 easy week at about half the sets (intensity kept); no date -> the normal stairway or year; after the event the plan ends and the user builds the next (R3-PER-01)

family_overlays.shared_rules_v1_1: Rules shared by every family (COACH-ANSWER unless marked): core opens the session light, 2 exercises x 2 sets short of failure, movable, with core supersets or monster sets allowed anywhere (ATH-11; COACH-R2 R2-SES-03); hip dominant + push and knee dominant + pull (UNI-11, ORD-06); heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days, non-axial hinge / leg press / belt squat on the other lower days (COACH-R2 R2-SES-01, R2-SES-02); horizontal pull before vertical (ORD-01); power before strength (ORD-03); warm-up always (ORD-08); 5-7 resistance exercises on split days, field athletes off-season up to 12 + the 2-exercise core block (VOL-08; COACH-R2 R2-SES-04); full-body days 2-4 exercises per muscle, never 1, so they run longer (about 7-10 resistance exercises, 55-80 min; 'it might be a little longer day', COACH-R2 R2-SES-05; 12_volume_algorithm v1.1 §3.10); calves 3 sets each leg day, rear delts own sets (VOL-17; COACH-R2 R2-VOL-04); optional days separate or add-on, ideally separate (ORD-10); default exercise per slot with a same-category dropdown and one-detail variations only (GEN-04; COACH-R2 R2-LIB-01); rotation bias kept both ways every week (COACH-R2 R2-LIB-03); cardio sessions adjustable up or down by the user (COACH-R2 R2-SES-06); 60+: Olympic lifts, plyos and depth jumps off by default, opt-in with the warning (COACH-R2 R2-ATH-08); no bands or variable resistance (EQ-01, EQ-12).
family_overlays.shared_rules_v1_2: Rules shared by every family (COACH-ANSWER unless marked): core opens the session light, 2 exercises x 2 sets short of failure, movable, with core supersets or monster sets allowed anywhere (ATH-11; COACH-R2 R2-SES-03); hip dominant + push and knee dominant + pull (UNI-11, ORD-06); heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days, non-axial hinge / leg press / belt squat on the other lower days (COACH-R2 R2-SES-01, R2-SES-02); horizontal pull before vertical (ORD-01); power before strength (ORD-03); warm-up always (ORD-08); 5-7 resistance exercises on split days, field athletes off-season up to 12 + the 2-exercise core block (VOL-08; COACH-R2 R2-SES-04), with 2-4 exercises for each group trained that day: the cross pattern (default for most athletes) leaves 2 jump / throw stations + 1 Olympic lift, the same-pattern athletic template (size-focused and high-level athletes) 3-4 jump stations + 1 Olympic lift (COACH-R3 R3-SES-01); full-body days 2-4 exercises per muscle, never 1, so they run longer (about 7-10 resistance exercises, 55-80 min; 'it might be a little longer day', COACH-R2 R2-SES-05; 12_volume_algorithm v1.2 §3.10); calves one exercise x 3 sets each leg day (COACH-R3 R3-SES-01); rear-delt work inside the shoulders group - not a muscle with its own floor, users / coaches can add more (VOL-17; COACH-R3 R3-VOL-01); optional days separate or add-on, ideally separate (ORD-10); default exercise per slot with a same-category dropdown and one-detail variations only (GEN-04; COACH-R2 R2-LIB-01); rotation bias kept both ways every week (COACH-R2 R2-LIB-03); cardio sessions adjustable up or down by the user (COACH-R2 R2-SES-06); 60+: landing drills (step down and stick, no bounce), balance, quick stepping without a hop, light medball throws and fast machine work ON; low ankle hops, other jumps, Olympic lifts and depth jumps OFF and switchable with the warning 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means'; overhead and low-bar squats out; snatch variants out (EQ-03) (COACH-R2 R2-ATH-08; COACH-R3 R3-ATH-02); no bands or variable resistance (EQ-01, EQ-12). v1.2 (round 3): counting on focus groups: hips = glutes + hamstrings (e.g. RDL + hip thrust + leg curl = 3 hip exercises), shoulders = front + side + rear delts (rear delts are not a muscle with its own floor; users and coaches can add more rear-delt work); 2-4 exercises per group trained that day; calves one exercise x 3 sets per leg day; Focus muscle 1 / 2 (optional, max 2) get +1 to +3 weekly sets each inside the stairway (COACH-R3 R3-SES-01, R3-VOL-01); the user or coach can switch off a day's athletic block or core block, add or remove exercises or whole blocks, and the plan recommends supersets to save time (COACH-R3 R3-SES-02); when the chosen days and minutes cannot hold the minimums, the plan (1) says so up front and offers another day or longer sessions, (2) if the time stays, trains fewer groups directly (big movers first; arms, calves and shoulder isolation from compound credit) instead of every group under the floor, (3) recommends supersets, and (4) keeps the stairway climbing on the groups it trains - never flat (COACH-R3 R3-SES-02; algorithm in 12_volume_algorithm / 05 v1.2).

volume_governor.statement_verbatim_paraphrase: People do ~15-20 sets per muscle per week; more for a muscle they want to grow, fewer with injury/pain. Volume ramps gradually week by week in ~3 %, 5 % or 7 % increments depending on the size of the muscle and the logic behind it.
volume_governor.observed_realization: The coach never writes a 3 % step. He writes whole-set steps (+25-50 % per step every 2-3 weeks) whose long-run compounded average is 4-6 %/week in his 12-week products, 2.6-3.8 %/week in the late pre-season and 3.8 %/week in the boxing conversion. The % rule is the long-run average of the step schedule (OBSERVED numbers, INFERRED reading).
volume_governor.tier_rationale: INFERRED: with typical weekly volumes in the coach's templates (quads ~16-18, chest/delts ~9-12, biceps/calves ~6-12), 3 % / 5 % / 7 % translate into about +0.35-0.85 set per muscle per week (chest/back 12 x 3 % = 0.36, quads/hams 18 x 3 % = 0.54, delts/triceps 9-12 x 5 % = 0.45-0.6, calves 6 x 7 % = 0.42, biceps 12 x 7 % = 0.84; rear delts 3 x 7 % = 0.21) = roughly +1 set every 1-3 weeks. That reproduces the observed cadence ('+1 set every 2-3 weeks') and the science that large muscles cost more systemic fatigue per set while small muscles recover faster. The REVERSE mapping (big = 7 %) would add ~1.3 sets/week to quads and ~0.36 to biceps, which matches nothing in the sheets. Coach to confirm.

volume_governor.counting: 1 hard set = 1.0 to each prime mover + 0.5 to each clear synergist (fractional method; matches Pelland 2025). Athletic sets (plyo, throws, sprints, Olympic) are counted as EXPOSURE, not as hypertrophy sets (open question).
algorithm: 1. base_m = weekly hard sets the template gives muscle m in week 1 (plus Focus slots).
2. rate_m = tier rate after modifiers; ceiling_m = 20 (26 if focus); if base_m >= ceiling_m: hold.
3. For each loading week: target_m(w) = min(ceiling_m, target_m(w-1) * (1 + rate_m)).
4. planned_m(w) = floor(target_m(w)) (never below base_m): a whole set is released only when the accumulated increment reaches 1.0.
5. Deload week: planned = round(0.6 x previous planned) (coach range -25 % to -50 %) and the template's deload dose (3 x 8).
6. After a mid-block deload (12-week plans) the target restarts at the week-4 value of wave 1 (observed: STRENGTH-12 wk8 = wk3/4 dose; AESTHETICS-12 wk8 = 4 sets = wk4-6).

7. Assign each released set to a slot by priority: (a) the muscle's Focus slot if focus; (b) the isolation slot for SMALL/MEDIUM muscles, (c) the primary bilateral compound for LARGE muscles in hypertrophy/strength, (d) never exceed the per-slot cap (4 fat loss, 5 hypertrophy, 6-7 strength main lift) or ~20 working sets / 7-10 exercises per session.

8. Small muscles may realise the same % through reps instead of sets (FAT BURN leg ext/curl slot 15 -> 20 -> 40 -> 40; Plotkin 2022 shows rep progression is as effective as load progression, but in lower-body exercises, so it does not by itself justify a small-muscle-only rule).

retired_v0.generator_pseudocode:
generate_plan(client):
  family   = map_goal(client.goal)            # HYPERTROPHY | STRENGTH | FAT_LOSS | HYBRID | GENERAL_BEGINNER | ATHLETE
  phase    = client.season_phase if family == ATHLETE else None   # OFF | PRE | IN | TRANSITION
  shape    = SKELETONS[family(+phase)][client.weeks]              # 6 / 8 / 12 week rows (role, volume_index, reps, effort, load, methods)
  template = choose_slot_template(family, client.days, client.sport, client.equipment)   # e.g. AESTHETICS 4-day, ATHLETIC 4-day, PPL 6-day
  base     = level_base(client.level)          # sets/exercise 2 (beginner) / 3 (intermediate+); athlete level dial for ATHLETE
  for week in shape:
     for slot in template.slots:
        ex      = pick_exercise(slot, tier=slot_tier[slot], variation=variation_rule(family, phase, week), history)
        sets    = base * week.volume_index/100  (STEP mode)  -> rounded, capped per slot (4 FL / 5 HYP / 6-7 STR main)
        reps    = week.reps[ex.class]            # compound wave vs isolation rule (inverse legend)
        effort  = EFFORT_BY_CLASS[ex.class] adjusted by week.effort
        load    = week.load if family == STRENGTH or ex.is_olympic else implicit
     apply_governor(SMOOTH mode for focus muscles; ceilings 20 / 26; pain/deficit/in-season modifiers)
     add_athletic_block(week.plyo_zone, contacts target, throws, sprint density)   # ATHLETE / HYBRID
     add_conditioning(aerobic level unlock, density progression, separate days)
     if week.role == DELOAD: apply D4 (3 x 8, RPE 7, drop methods/conditioning/Oly, Part A 1-2 sets)
  after each logged week: autoregulate(EFFORT, HOW IT FELT?) -> adjust next week; early deload if D11 fires

athletic_quality_rules_v1_1.rule: Own budget: plyos, ballistics, throws, Olympic lifts and sprints never count toward muscle sets; counted as contacts, reps, throws, meters.

Ballistic -> plyometric inside every block; plyometric share at the END of a block by sport (sprinters 75 %; volleyball, soccer, football skill 60 %; basketball, tennis, football big-skill, weekend warriors 50 %; baseball, softball, hockey, linemen, MMA 40 %; boxing, karate, kickboxing, wrestling, BJJ, golf 25 %); each block starts 15 points more ballistic. Ballistic = longer contact or one big effort (squat, box, broad, loaded/hex-bar jumps, medball throws); plyometric = short bouncy contacts (pogo/ankle hops, hurdle hops, depth jumps, bounds, squirrel jumps, repeated jumps).
athletic_quality_rules_v1_1.tag: COACH-ANSWER CAT-10, ATH-01, ATH-02; COACH-R2 R2-ATH-01, R2-ATH-02

athletic_quality_rules_v1_1.rule: Receive-Create stages (not zones): RC1 Land (receive and pause, stick the landing) -> RC2 Land & Go (receive, then create once) -> RC3 Repeat (repeated receive/create). 12-week: weeks 1-3 / 4-7 / 8-12; 8-week: 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8; other lengths in proportion (PROPOSED). Restart at RC1 each off-season; hold the stage in maintenance blocks (pre-season included); intermediate and advanced athletes may start at RC2. Bilateral before unilateral inside each stage. Davidson zones do not apply to plyos.

Olympic lifts for everyone in athletic training, up to 4 days a week (clean days = squat pattern, snatch days = hinge pattern); weight by RIR/RPE and speed unless a tested max; full lifts 3-5 reps per set; in-season light 2 x 3 dropped in heavy game weeks; youth from the floor from ~14 after a hang block.
athletic_quality_rules_v1_1.tag: COACH-ANSWER ATH-10, LIB-07, LIB-13; COACH-R2 R2-ATH-04, R2-ATH-05, R2-ATH-08, R2-GEN-06

athletic_quality_rules_v1_1.rule: Throws: no levels; light balls (8-10 lb) for speed, never over 20 lb; none for aesthetics/bodybuilders except warm-up.
Contrast / French contrast / complexes: intermediate+ athletes, off-season only, heavy lift ~78-85 %.

In-season: sprints for speed athletes, jumps for jumping athletes, strength maintenance for others; game-heavy sports (basketball, volleyball, soccer, football, hockey): gym plyos ~half, no extra COD, sprints only for speed athletes, hard gym day >= 48 h before a game.

Older adults (60+): no Olympic lifts, plyos or depth jumps by default; landing drills (stick the landing: the 'receive' stage, not a plyo by R2-ATH-02) stay in; low ankle hops, other plyos, Olympic variants and depth jumps are an option only, with the warning 'Make sure that you have a fitness professional to help you understand what this means.' RESOLUTION FLAGGED: the approved proposal kept 'landing drills and low ankle hops'; his text says no plyos by default and ankle hops are plyometric by his own list (R2-ATH-02), so ankle hops became opt-in; depth jumps were 'never' in round 1 (ATH-09, EQ-03) and are now a coach-guided option at most.
Change of direction: route tiers EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN for every athlete; no extra COD in-season for game-heavy sports.

Aerobic: general/fat loss 3; aesthetics 4 (a 2nd easy Orange) + optional walks; athletes off-season 2-4 by sport, pre-season 2, in-season 2; powerlifters 2 easy Orange; the user can add or remove sessions.
No bands: reverse-banded plyos and banded throws/chops are out of scope.

exercise_progression_rules_v1_1.rule: Exercise blocks of 4-6 weeks inside a training block (12-week: 1-4 / 5-8 / 9-12; 8-week: 1-4 / 5-8): exercises fixed inside; the next exercise block changes one or two small details (grip, stance, implement, range of motion, rep range), never all at once.
Variations are one-detail changes of library exercises, shown as e.g. 'Reverse lunge - dumbbell in opposite hand'; the generator never invents an exercise.
A/B lead-lift weeks (squat-led / hinge-led; bench / overhead) only for people who want variety; off by default.
Second exposure of a slot in a week = a different exercise from the same category.

Spine: heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days (e.g. squat Monday, deadlift Friday); non-axial hinge (hip thrust, back extension, reverse hyper) and leg press or belt squat on the other lower days. Axial = barbell back, front, zercher, overhead and Smith squats; barbell or trap-bar deadlifts and RDLs; good mornings. Not axial = leg press, belt squat, hip thrust, back extension, reverse hyper, single-leg DB work, Olympic lifts, loaded jumps. Goblet, hack squat and pendulum are fine on the second day if not sore. Powerlifters may add a light technique squat or deadlift.

headline_rules_v1: R1 Five plan modes, chosen at intake: 12-week cycle (his preferred), 8-week, 4-6-week maintenance/transition, open-ended week-by-week, and yearly. No 6-week loading plan. (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; GEN-02 (intake))

R2 12-week cycle = 2-4 weeks acclimation ('getting used to the movements') -> 4-6 weeks driving hard, not all the way to the top -> last weeks hardest (more tired, more stimulus). Default split 3 / 6 / 3 weeks; L1 or returning 4 / 5 / 3; L3 2 / 6 / 4 (so the drive stays inside his '4 to 6 weeks'). (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; split PROPOSED)

R3 8-week plan = 'a program that wants to modify you, so you have to start hard': start about 10 % above the level start, weeks 1-4 adapting, weeks 5-8 driving hard. (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; +10 % PROPOSED)

R4 4-6-week blocks are maintenance/transition (vacation 1-2 weeks, travel, moving, off-season -> in-season, planned maintenance) at about 50-70 % of the volume, to recover and not push. (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; SCIENCE (Bickel 2011, Bosquet 2013, Ogasawara 2013))
R5 Repeated 12-week cycles start one level higher ('start at a 2 and end at an 11'): next start = previous start x 1.05, cap + 1 set. (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; step size PROPOSED)

R6 Volume moves by the person, not by muscle size: each week 3, 5 or 7 % of each muscle's weekly sets, chosen from fatigue, life and response; 10 %/week is too much; fractions are banked and released as whole sets on the first exercise of the day first. (COACH-ANSWER VOL-04, VOL-05, UNI-05, VOL-06, VOL-07)

R7 Smooth weekly increases for hypertrophy and general clients; 2-week steps and waves for fight or competition prep; the confirmed strength %-template (80/80/85/85/90/90 %, RPE 7 -> 10; Olympic 75 -> 90 % in 4 weeks) is the step pattern for main lifts. (COACH-ANSWER PER-10, PER-09)

R8 Blocks of 4-6 weeks: same exercises inside a block, 1-2 small variable changes at the next block; A/B lead-lift weeks only for clients who want variety; the second weekly exposure of a slot is a different exercise and only one axial-loading day a week. (COACH-ANSWER PER-02, PER-03, PER-04)

R9 Deload = about half the sets, same exercises, lighter or 3+ RIR, no buy-outs or finishers. Not planned at a fixed week: triggered by the logs, used as week 1 of the next cycle, or replaced by a maintenance block. (COACH-ANSWER PER-05; placement PROPOSED)
R10 A slot moves up a level at the end of a block when it felt '8 - That was perfect' or easier with no pain. (COACH-ANSWER PER-06)
R11 Tests are chosen by checkbox at the start of a block (or 'No need for testing'); the plan schedules them at the end of the block and reminds the client. (COACH-ANSWER PER-07)

R12 Athletes: off-season most volume (VOL 1 -> VOL 2 -> VOL 3, one per block; STARTING/MID/ADVANCED as blocks or levels by need); pre-season more speed/power, less volume; in-season 2 days, low volume, minimal bilateral; post-season recovery. (COACH-ANSWER PER-08, PER-11, PRG-04, UNI-10)
R13 Effort is written in RIR, 1-3 RIR at all times; 'MAX' only on small-muscle or bodyweight work; the hardest weeks sit at 1 RIR. (COACH-ANSWER VOL-13, GEN-08; ramp PROPOSED)

R14 Athletic work has its own budget (never muscle sets): programs start ballistic and become plyometric through receive & pause -> receive then create -> repeated stages; everyone in athletic training gets an Olympic-lift variant. (COACH-ANSWER VOL-10, CAT-10, CAT-11, ATH-10)
R15 The plan adjusts week to week from logged EFFORT and HOW IT FELT (pain -> swap or cut; EFFORT 9-10 -> hold or cut; EFFORT <= 6 -> add). (COACH-ANSWER GEN-05)
