ambiguities: He says 'this second half of the year, the second quarter': the text describes April-June, but 'second half' would be July-December. We read Q2 = April-June.

Q2 is described two ways: 'losing body fat and starting to get in shape' and 'a mix in between building up a little bit more muscle and keeping your body fat down'. Q1 is also a cut ('start the year cutting down'). Which quarter carries the main fat-loss phase: Q1, Q2 or both?

'Maintaining' in Q3: the 50-70 % maintenance volume of PER-01, or the 15-20-set 'maintenance to a little bit of growth' band of UNI-01? Our proposal (the level start) is about 66-80 % of the previous peak, so it satisfies both readings.

'Really hard work' in Q1 while cutting: should volume still step up a level in a calorie deficit? Research says a deficit blunts muscle gain but not strength gain (Murphy & Koehler 2022), so we hold the level start and put the extra work into cardio and density.

The calendar is northern-hemisphere and Christmas-based. Spanish-speaking users in the southern hemisphere (Argentina, Chile, Uruguay) have summer in December-February, and other holidays (Semana Santa, Thanksgiving, a personal vacation) may matter more.

athletic_quality_rules_v1.rule: Own budget: plyos, ballistics, throws, Olympic lifts and sprints never count toward muscle sets; counted as contacts, reps, throws, meters

Ballistic -> plyometric: programs start more ballistic and become more plyometric (connective tissue). Plyo:ballistic share by the sport's ground-contact time: more ground time (karate, fighters) -> more ballistics; less (sprinters) -> more plyos; basketball a mix; baseball ballistics + rotational + sprinting, few plyos
athletic_quality_rules_v1.tag: COACH-ANSWER CAT-10, ATH-01, ATH-02; shares PROPOSED (12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.13)

athletic_quality_rules_v1.rule: Plyo method stages (not zones): stage 1 receive & pause, stage 2 receive then create once, stage 3 repeatedly receive and create; bilateral before unilateral (unilateral is harder). Name pending; PROPOSED 'Receive-Create stages' RC1-RC3, weeks 1-2 / 3-5 / 6+ of a cycle (12-week off-season: RC3 bilateral weeks 6-8, unilateral weeks 9-12). Davidson zones do not apply to plyos

Olympic lifts for everyone in athletic training: L1 DB/KB snatches, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls/cleans; L2+ hang power -> full 'Squat Snatch' / 'Squat Clean' / 'Squat Clean & Jerk'; push press easier, push jerk intermediate/advanced; youth may lift from the floor; % ramp 75 -> 90 % per 4-week block for L2+. In-season: open question
athletic_quality_rules_v1.tag: COACH-ANSWER ATH-10, LIB-07, LIB-13, ATH-09, PER-09

athletic_quality_rules_v1.rule: Throws: no levels; light balls (8-10 lb) for speed, never over 20 lb; none for aesthetics/bodybuilders except warm-up; high volume for baseball, boxing, MMA, tennis, golf
Contrast / French contrast / complexes: intermediate+ athletes, off-season only, heavy lift ~78-85 %, no rest inside the complex (fight-camp use: round-2 question)
In-season athletic work: sprints for speed athletes, (high) jumps for jumping athletes, strength maintenance for others
Older clients: few plyos unless they ask; no sex-based rules (age, foundation, goal, injuries decide)
Change of direction: route tiers EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN apply to every athlete

Aerobic: 3 sessions/week general/fat loss, 2 athletes in-season, 4 aesthetics/bodybuilders plus long walks after workouts; off-season VO2/mitochondrial work can come from supersets; fighters' session-opening cardio is a real aerobic block; any erg, by calories, time or distance
No bands: reverse-banded (assisted/overspeed) plyos and banded throws/chops are out of scope

exercise_progression_rules_v1.rule: Blocks of 4-6 weeks: exercises fixed inside a block; the next block changes one or two of grip, stance, implement, range of motion or rep range, never all at once
A/B lead-lift weeks (squat-led / hinge-led; bench / overhead) are an option for people who want variety, in any program; off by default

Second exposure of a slot in a week = a different exercise from the same category; axial spinal loading once a week (squat one day, leg press or belt squat the other; deadlifts count as spinal loading)

Level up a slot at the end of a block if it felt '8 - That was perfect' or easier with no pain; levels are still theoretical; client level and exercise level are separate; a higher level keeps the lower options

Exercise level reads from skill, stability and load position: front-loaded/low = foundational, load on the body/horizontal = intermediate, behind the body/overhead = advanced; machines and cables are easier

Choice between alternatives: by client profile (older/injured -> machines or DBs; experienced -> barbell) and by the client's preference. Machines are NOT ranked (brands and angles differ): hack squat and leg press are more constrained than the Smith machine; belt squat avoids axial loading (use it when the back is already loaded or sore); GHD / reverse hyper if available and the client feels the right muscles

Older / injured / high-volume clients collect volume on constrained machines (constraint 4-5) and never get overhead squat, snatch, low-bar squat or depth jumps; they may use machines filed at any level

Bilateral:unilateral share across blocks: bodybuilders/powerlifters ~50/50 in block 1 with contra/ipsi health work in the first 2-4 weeks -> 80/20-90/10; field/COD athletes 80-90 % unilateral; in-season minimal bilateral; adjustable 90/10 to 10/90; pain shifts it
exercise_progression_rules_v1.tag: COACH-ANSWER UNI-02, UNI-03, UNI-10, CAT-13; profile numbers PROPOSED (12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.11)

exercise_progression_rules_v1.rule: Contralateral load pulls into the hip (change-of-direction athletes: football, soccer, basketball, tennis); ipsilateral helps out of the hip (sprint acceleration: ipsilateral step-ups)
Pain: swap within the category to a more constrained, split-grip or unilateral variant and keep the sets if possible; then cut 30-50 %; then drop the exercise
No bands or variable resistance (bands, chains, weight releasers) in any variation or substitution

autoregulation_v1.action: HOLD: rate 0 % for everyone next week
autoregulation_v1.tag: COACH-ANSWER GEN-05 ('EFFORT 9-10 -> hold or cut sets')

autoregulation_v1.signal: Median weekly EFFORT <= 6 ('6 - Broke a Sweat' or easier)
autoregulation_v1.action: ADD: at least 5 %, and raise load or reps first

autoregulation_v1.signal: EFFORT 7-8 ('7 - That was tough' / '8 - That was perfect') with sessions done
autoregulation_v1.action: rate from the readiness score R = 0.40 effort + 0.20 completion + 0.20 performance + 0.20 life: >= 85 -> 7 %, 70-84 -> 5 %, 55-69 -> 3 %, < 55 -> hold
autoregulation_v1.tag: COACH-ANSWER VOL-05 (by the person); score PROPOSED (12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.7)

autoregulation_v1.action: next exposure: swap inside the category to a more constrained, split-grip or unilateral variant, keep the sets if possible; again -> that slot -30-50 %, muscle rate 0; a third time -> drop the exercise for the block and flag for the coach

autoregulation_v1.signal: HOW IT FELT? 'Felt the WRONG muscle'
autoregulation_v1.action: change one variable inside the same category; volume unchanged
regress one exercise level or use an assisted version; volume unchanged

autoregulation_v1.signal: HOW IT FELT? 'Felt the RIGHT muscles' + '8 - That was perfect' or easier through the block, no pain
autoregulation_v1.action: slot moves up one level at the next block

autoregulation_v1.signal: 2 weeks of hold in a row, or the D6 triggers
autoregulation_v1.action: deload next week (about half the sets)
the whole plan uses the intake rate (default 5 %; 3 % if stressed, older, returning or in pain; never 7 % before logs)

retired_v1.generator_pseudocode_v1:
generate_plan(client):                                   # v1 (coach answers applied)
  level  = level_from_experience(years, months_off, ex_pro)   # L1/L2/L3 (PRG-05)
  family = map_goal(goal)       # HYPERTROPHY | STRENGTH | FAT_LOSS | GENERAL | HYBRID | ATHLETE (sport, position, season)
  mode   = client.plan_mode     # C12 | C8 | MAINT(4-6, reason) | WBW | YEAR | PREP(date) | SEASON   (PER-01, PER-08, PER-10)
  output = client.output_mode   # static | adaptive (PROPOSED: GEN-03 vs GEN-05)
  tests  = client.test_ticks    # strength / cardio / speed / jumps / body, or 'No need for testing' (PER-07)

  grid    = MODE_GRID[mode](level)            # week -> phase (ACCLIMATION/ADAPT, DRIVE, HARDEST, MAINTAIN, DELOAD, TEST), rate cap, RIR band, block number
  overlay = FAMILY_OVERLAY[family]            # phase -> reps, effort, load, methods, laterality, conditioning, athletic stage
  targets = volume_engine_v1.start(level, family, season, priorities, pain)   # 12_volume_algorithm_v1 §3.3-3.6
  if mode == C8:    targets *= 1.10                                           # 'start hard' (PROPOSED size)
  if mode == MAINT: targets = factor(reason, age) * mean(last_block[-4:])     # 50-70 % (PER-01)
  if previous_cycle == 'productive': start *= 1.05; cap += 1                  # 'start at a 2, end at an 11'

  week_1 = build_sessions(targets, template(family, days, minutes))  # core first; hip+push / knee+pull; one axial day; 5-7 exercises (10-12 field athletes)
  for week in grid:
      if week.role == DELOAD: emit(half_sets(previous_week)); continue        # PER-05
      rate = min(week.rate_cap, plan_rate if output == static else readiness_rate(logs))   # VOL-05, GEN-05; person total < 10 %/week (UNI-05), stagger releases (PROPOSED)
      if mode == PREP or (family == STRENGTH and lift is main): apply_steps(week)          # PER-10, PER-09
      else: bank_and_place(rate)                                                       # VOL-06, VOL-07
      apply overlay[week.phase] -> reps, RIR, %, methods (MYO last isolation; supersets as fatigue tool; contrast off-season int+)
      athletic block (own budget, VOL-10): plyo:ballistic share by sport, method stage 1 -> 2 -> 3, Olympic variant by level
      if week.block_boundary: change 1-2 small variables; rebalance bilateral share; level-up eligible slots   # PER-02, PER-06, UNI-02
      if week.is_last and tests: schedule test day, cut the rest of that week, send reminders                # PER-07
      if triggers(logs): next week = DELOAD                                                                 # D6
  after the plan: deload week 1 of next cycle | maintenance block | yearly next quarter
open_questions_round2_v1: Yearly mode (PER-01): (a) you said 'this second half of the year, the second quarter'; we read Q2 = April-June, right? (b) Is Q2 a fat-loss quarter continuing Q1's cut, or a lean-gain quarter ('build a little more muscle and keep fat down')? Which quarter carries the main cut? (c) Is Q3 'maintain' the 50-70 % maintenance volume or your 15-20-set 'maintenance to a little growth' band? (d) In the Q1 cut, should volume still step up a level, or hold while the extra work comes from cardio?

Yearly calendar: fixed months (northern-hemisphere summer, Christmas/New Year) or the user's own summer, event date and holidays (southern-hemisphere users, Semana Santa, Thanksgiving, personal vacations)? Should athletes in yearly mode follow their season calendar instead of quarters?

Deloads in your 12-week shape: you rejected the week-7 mid deload, yet STRENGTH-12 ('MID DELOAD') and AESTHETICS-12 ('A WEEK LOWER') both have one. Planned at a fixed week, only when the person needs it, or as week 1 of the next cycle?

Season change: PER-01 lists 'transitioning from off-season to on-season' as a 4-6-week maintenance use, and PER-08 describes pre-season as less volume, more speed/power. Is pre-season that same block (maintenance-level lifting + speed/power), or are they separate?

'12/10/8 -20' (PRG-07): the light 20 is an extra set. In AESTHETICS-12 the SETS row says 3 next to '12/10/8 -20' (weeks 1-3) but 4 next to '12/12/10-20' (weeks 4-6). Does the light 20 count inside SETS or on top, and does it count as a hard set?

In-season Olympic lifts: ATH-10 says everyone in athletic training gets Olympic lifts, but BASEBALL Block 3 (in-season) has none and PER-08 says in-season = sprints, strength maintenance or jumps. Keep a light Olympic/power piece in-season, or none?

Contrast/complexes are off-season only (ATH-12), but the BASEBALL Block 2 complexes ('5 of each') sit in a block we had read as pre-season. Is Block 2 late off-season (VOL 3), and do complexes stop when pre-season begins? The same question for fight camps: your 'EXAMPLE BOXING 8 WEEK BUILD UP' uses complexes from week 3, and we use it as the fight-prep pattern (PER-10). Does a fight camp count as 'off-season' for complexes, or should a camp drop them?

'Start at a 2 and end at an 11' for advanced clients already at the 25-set ceiling: should 'one level higher' then mean heavier loads and intensifiers, rotating priority muscles (cap ~30), or a personal cap learned from their logs?

PRG-04 ('depends on whatever is needed'): proposed rule = an off-season of 16+ weeks for an L1-L2 athlete runs STARTING -> MID -> ADVANCED as consecutive blocks; a shorter off-season or an L3 athlete gets the template that matches their level. OK?

Olympic ramp (PER-09, you asked us to make sure it is correct): 4 x 6 @ 80-85 % and 4 x 4 @ 90 % match common power guidance, but 4 x 8 @ 75 % is more reps per set than usual for full catch lifts (squat clean, squat snatch), where technique fades late in a set. Keep 8s for DB/KB and hang-pull/hang-power variants and use 3-5-rep sets for the full lifts (same weekly reps), or keep 4 x 8 for everything? And is the % taken from the 1RM of that exact variant (hang clean, power clean)?

8-week plan (PER-01): you said 'the first 4 weeks ... getting used to it, then the next 4 weeks ... driving it hard', and also 'you want good stimulus for the last 5 weeks' and 'you have to start hard'. Is it 4 + 4 or 3 + 5? And does 'start hard' mean more weekly sets than a 12-week start (we propose +10 %), harder effort (2 RIR from week 1), or both?

Week-by-week mode (PER-01: 'just keep me in line ... and then it does it by itself') can only adjust if the person reports how the week went. You also said people should track on their own (GEN-03). Is a 30-second weekly check-in (sessions done, effort, any pain, sleep/stress) acceptable for this mode, while fixed 8- and 12-week plans can be used without any tracking?

changes.change: No check-ins, no tracking, no adaptive inputs: the generator outputs the whole plan once with its planned stairway and people and coaches adjust it themselves ('I want them to be able to kick out a program, and that's it'). Retired: the optional weekly check-in and its step table (+2 points if too easy, hold on 9, hold and -1 set after a 10, 'failed', repeat the week), the block-at-risk offer (D6 signals), D13 repeat week, the week-by-week mode (it ran on the weekly check-in) and the 'level up if it felt like an 8' read from logs (now the person's or coach's call when they build the next block).

Stairway approved: about 3 % a week until the halfway week, about 5 % after, each trained group reaching its ceiling in the last week (λ); effort cue 3 RIR -> 2 -> 1-2 -> 1 + intensifiers in the last week, always inside 1-3 RIR. Step sizes, λ, halves and the RIR drift move from PROPOSED to approved; the printed 2-11 stair-level number stays a PROPOSED display.

The easy week after a completed block is an extra week (12 + 1 = a 13-week quarter in the year plan) and only a RECOMMENDATION, not mandatory; when a block ends it ends and the user goes back into the app to build what comes next (next block, maintenance or another plan); the end-of-maintenance prompt is replaced by the plan ending. Approved 14.3 #2.

Holiday and vacation weeks are planned between blocks; a week marked after a block has started ends that block (stop -> maintenance -> new block) unless the mark is removed (approved 14.3 #1). The 'offer to stop a block' from check-in signals lapses with the check-ins: stopping is the person's or coach's call.

Nothing is stored: test reminders become lines printed in the plan (block start, 7 days and 1 day before the test day); starting the next block one step up needs an intake answer ('I just finished a block') instead of a stored history (PROPOSED).

Swimming: a 2-week dryland taper lined up with the swim coach's taper before the main championship meet; 1 week or none before smaller meets (approved 14.3 #6). Swimming defaults in season type C: 3 dryland days + 1 optional (2 for younger or lower-level swimmers), 0 extra gym cardio, jumps mostly ballistic (25 % plyometric), Olympic lifts 2-3 days, shoulder care (external rotation, floor Y / T raises, KB face pulls) every session, never bands.

Plyometric shares of the remaining sports approved (75 % runners; 60 % lacrosse, field hockey, flag football, ultimate cutters, rugby sevens, high jump, pole vault, gymnastics, cheer flyers; 50 % beach volleyball, pickleball, padel, rugby backs, goalkeepers, javelin, HYROX; 40 % rugby forwards, cheer bases, throwers, diving, alpine skiing, cycling; 25 % swimming, water polo, rowing, judo, taekwondo, climbing); off-season cardio 2-4 like the round-2 list, 0 extra for swimmers, runners, rowers and endurance cyclists; the in-season game-heavy rule also for lacrosse, field hockey, rugby, ultimate, flag football and beach volleyball; recreational players use their activity's share ('a bit of everything' 50 %).

Stay athletic and active approved: the user can enter play days - the hardest gym day stays at least 48 h before the biggest play day, and weeks with 3+ play sessions drop the extra agility drills and half the jumps; a 45-60+ minute session of the activity counts as one of the 3 cardio sessions (up to 2); optional event date - the hardest weeks end 1 week before, then 1 easy week at about half the sets (approved 14.3 #5).
changes.where: §6 D8, §7.0 PREP, §8.1 GENERAL, §8.2.6; JSON plan_length_model.event_peak_genpop, athlete.stay_athletic_active

changes.change: HYROX plan approved: 2 strength days (squat + pull, deadlift + push) + 2 hybrid days (run intervals, or 1 km run + 1 station repeated); 4 cardio sessions (Blue, Green, Orange + a second Orange); 2 short station circuits a week as finishers that never count as muscle sets; wall balls with the race ball (<= 20 lb); 40-rep / AMRAP sets only inside these circuits; jumps 50 % plyometric. A race date uses the R3-ATH-05 event peak.

Older adults (60+): landing drills, balance, quick stepping without a hop, light medball throws and fast machine work ON; low ankle hops, other jumps, Olympic lifts and depth jumps OFF and switchable with the warning; overhead and low-bar squats out (snatches stay out under EQ-03). Pickleball, padel and tennis players 50+: knee-friendly strength, calf and Achilles work every leg day, rotator-cuff work, low-impact jumps only unless switched on.

Rear delts are part of the shoulders group (no own floor; users and coaches can add more); counting on focus groups (hips = glutes + hamstrings, shoulders = front + side + rear delts); calves one exercise x 3 sets per leg day; Focus muscle 1 / 2 at intake, +1 to +3 weekly sets each inside the stairway; the stairway climbs on groups.

Plan editing and time: the user or coach can switch off a day's athletic or core block and add or remove exercises or whole blocks; supersets are recommended; when the time cannot hold the minimums the plan says so up front, offers another day or longer sessions, then trains fewer groups directly (big movers first), recommends supersets and keeps the stairway climbing on the trained groups. The time structure is unchanged: switching blocks off never flattens or shortens the stairway.

Placement approved: an added set alternates between the two exposures of the same day type; extra small-muscle sets become a short bonus exercise on the optional day, or on a day that already trains that muscle, never as that day's only exercise for it.

athletic_quality_rules_v1_2.rule: Own budget: plyos, ballistics, throws, Olympic lifts and sprints never count toward muscle sets; counted as contacts, reps, throws, meters.

Ballistic -> plyometric inside every block; plyometric share at the END of a block by sport (sprinters 75 %; volleyball, soccer, football skill 60 %; basketball, tennis, football big-skill, weekend warriors 50 %; baseball, softball, hockey, linemen, MMA 40 %; boxing, karate, kickboxing, wrestling, BJJ, golf 25 %; v1.2 the remaining sports: runners 75 %; lacrosse, field hockey, flag football, ultimate cutters, rugby sevens, high jump, pole vault, gymnastics, cheer flyers 60 %; beach volleyball, pickleball, padel, rugby backs, goalkeepers, javelin, HYROX 50 %; rugby forwards, cheer bases, throwers, diving, alpine skiing, cycling 40 %; swimming, water polo, rowing, judo, taekwondo, climbing 25 %; recreational players use their activity's share, 'a bit of everything' 50 %); each block starts 15 points more ballistic. Ballistic = longer contact or one big effort (squat, box, broad, loaded/hex-bar jumps, medball throws); plyometric = short bouncy contacts (pogo/ankle hops, hurdle hops, depth jumps, bounds, squirrel jumps, repeated jumps).

athletic_quality_rules_v1_2.rule: Receive-Create stages (not zones): RC1 Land (receive and pause, stick the landing) -> RC2 Land & Go (receive, then create once) -> RC3 Repeat (repeated receive/create). 12-week: weeks 1-3 / 4-7 / 8-12; 8-week: 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8; other lengths in proportion (PROPOSED). Restart at RC1 each off-season; hold the stage in maintenance blocks (pre-season included); intermediate and advanced athletes may start at RC2. Bilateral before unilateral inside each stage. Davidson zones do not apply to plyos.

Olympic lifts for everyone in athletic training, up to 4 days a week (clean days = squat pattern, snatch days = hinge pattern); weight by RIR/RPE and speed unless a tested max; full lifts 3-5 reps per set; in-season light 2 x 3 dropped in heavy game weeks; youth from the floor from ~14 after a hang block.

In-season: sprints for speed athletes, jumps for jumping athletes, strength maintenance for others; game-heavy sports (basketball, volleyball, soccer, football, hockey; + lacrosse, field hockey, rugby, ultimate, flag football, beach volleyball - COACH-R3 R3-ATH-04): gym plyos ~half, no extra COD, sprints only for speed athletes, hard gym day >= 48 h before a game.

athletic_quality_rules_v1_2.rule: No bands: reverse-banded plyos and banded throws/chops are out of scope.

Swimming: 3 dryland days + 1 optional (2 for younger or lower-level swimmers), 0 extra gym cardio, jumps mostly ballistic (25 % plyometric at the end of a block), Olympic lifts 2-3 days, shoulder care every session (external rotation, floor Y / T raises, KB face pulls), never bands; swimmers: a 2-week dryland taper lined up with the swim coach's taper before the main championship meet; 1 week or none before smaller meets.

HYROX (approved, COACH-R3 R3-ATH-03): 2 strength days (squat + pull, deadlift + push) + 2 hybrid days (run intervals, or 1 km run + 1 station repeated); 4 cardio sessions (Blue, Green, Orange + a second Orange) because running is about half the race; 2 short station circuits a week (sled push / pull, burpee broad jumps, wall balls, farmers carry, sandbag lunges, SkiErg / row) as finishers that never count as muscle sets; wall balls with the race ball (never over 20 lb); 40-rep / AMRAP sets only inside these circuits; jumps 50 % plyometric; race date as the gen-pop event peak.

Stay-active users: play days (approved, COACH-R3 R3-ATH-05): the user can enter the days they play; the hardest gym day stays at least 48 h before the biggest play day; weeks with 3+ play sessions drop the extra agility drills and half the jumps; a day's athletic or core block can be switched off by the user or coach (e.g. sore calves after a lot of pickleball).

exercise_progression_rules_v1_2.rule: Exercise blocks of 4-6 weeks inside a training block (12-week: 1-4 / 5-8 / 9-12; 8-week: 1-4 / 5-8): exercises fixed inside; the next exercise block changes one or two small details (grip, stance, implement, range of motion, rep range), never all at once.
Variations are one-detail changes of library exercises, shown as e.g. 'Reverse lunge - dumbbell in opposite hand'; the generator never invents an exercise.
A/B lead-lift weeks (squat-led / hinge-led; bench / overhead) only for people who want variety; off by default.
Second exposure of a slot in a week = a different exercise from the same category.

Spine: heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days (e.g. squat Monday, deadlift Friday); non-axial hinge (hip thrust, back extension, reverse hyper) and leg press or belt squat on the other lower days. Axial = barbell back, front, zercher, overhead and Smith squats; barbell or trap-bar deadlifts and RDLs; good mornings. Not axial = leg press, belt squat, hip thrust, back extension, reverse hyper, single-leg DB work, Olympic lifts, loaded jumps. Goblet, hack squat and pendulum are fine on the second day if not sore. Powerlifters may add a light technique squat or deadlift.
exercise_progression_rules_v1_2.tag: COACH-R2 R2-SES-01, R2-SES-02; COACH-ANSWER PER-04, EQ-11

exercise_progression_rules_v1_2.rule: Level up a slot at the end of an exercise block if it felt '8 - That was perfect' or easier with no pain. Levels are still theoretical; client level and exercise level are separate; the level comes from load position, skill and stability (zone is only a tag). v1.2: nothing is logged (R3-VOL-02), so the person or coach makes this call when they build the next block; the printed plan says so.
exercise_progression_rules_v1_2.tag: COACH-ANSWER PER-06, CAT-04, CAT-05, CAT-06; COACH-R2 R2-LIB-02; COACH-R3 R3-VOL-02

exercise_progression_rules_v1_2.rule: Choice between alternatives: by client profile (older/injured -> machines or DBs; experienced -> barbell) and by preference; machines are not ranked; hack squat and leg press are more constrained than the Smith machine; belt squat avoids axial loading.

Bilateral:unilateral share across blocks: bodybuilders/powerlifters ~50/50 in block 1 (contra/ipsi health work in the first 2-4 weeks) -> 80/20-90/10; field/COD athletes 80-90 % unilateral; in-season minimal bilateral; pain shifts it.
Pain: swap within the category to a more constrained, split-grip or unilateral variant and keep the sets if possible; then cut 30-50 %; then drop the exercise.
KB face pulls are shoulder work (side/rear delts, traps), placed on pull or shoulder days; bench push-ups exist in both versions (hands on the bench = foundational, feet on the bench = advanced).
exercise_progression_rules_v1_2.tag: COACH-R2 R2-LIB-04, R2-LIB-05; COACH-ANSWER LIB-10, LIB-12

exercise_progression_rules_v1_2.rule: No bands, chains or variable resistance in any generator rule.

Rotation bias (Davidson zones): every week keeps both external-rotation (vertical, zones 1 and 3) and internal-rotation (horizontal, zone 2) work; the bias is used to pick swaps when something hurts; not set by sport for now. The zone is a tag on the exercise; it does not set the level.

headline_rules_v1_1: R1 Plan modes chosen at intake: 12-week block (his preferred), 8-week block, maintenance phase (length chosen, extendable), week-by-week (rolling stairways) and the yearly gen-pop plan; prep (event/fight date) and season (competitive athlete) are overlays. No 6-week loading plan. (COACH-ANSWER PER-01; COACH-R2 R2-PER-01, R2-PER-06)

R2 Every training block is a stairway: gradual weekly steps, smaller in the first weeks, a little bigger after the halfway point 'but not too much', hardest weeks last; 12-week: the last 4 weeks (9-12) are 'brutal'. It applies to every plan length. (COACH-R2 R2-PER-03, R2-PER-04)

R3 'Start at a 2, end at an 11' is how hard the week feels (overall volume and loading), not a set count: week 1 feels like a 2 and the last week like an 11, a little past the usual limits. Every week at least one dial climbs: a set, load or reps, or the RIR target. (COACH-R2 R2-PER-05; dial rule PROPOSED)

R4 Planned steps (PROPOSED numbers, the same as 12_volume_algorithm v1.1, which owns the set math): 3 % to halfway, then 5 %; when a muscle's cap would come early, all its steps shrink by one factor λ so the peak lands on the cap in the last week; older adults (60+) at most 3 %; never above 7 % planned; the person's total weekly sets rise < 10 %. Phases: 12-week ACCLIMATION 1-3 (L1 1-4, L3 1-2) -> DRIVE to week 8 -> HARDEST 9-12; 8-week ACCLIMATION 1-2 (L1 1-3, L3 1) -> DRIVE to week 5 -> HARDEST 6-8. (COACH-R2 R2-PER-03, R2-PER-04; COACH-ANSWER PER-01, UNI-05)

R5 No check-in = no adaptation: the plan runs its planned stairway (R2-VOL-03). The optional check-in decides the step from effort, completion and pain only: on target = planned step; too easy = planned step + 2 points (max 7 %); 9 = hold; 10 ('the max I could do, but successful') = hold and -1 set on that day; under half the sessions = repeat the week. No sleep, stress or life inputs anywhere. (COACH-R2 R2-VOL-01, R2-VOL-02, R2-VOL-03, R2-GEN-04; notch rule PROPOSED)
R6 No deload or maintenance week inside a block: blocks are completed. Someone who cannot complete a block cancels it -> maintenance phase -> a whole new block from week 1. (COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07)

R7 Between two completed blocks: one recovery week at about half the sets of the hardest week, same exercises, 3+ RIR; none after a maintenance phase; maintenance at the end of a block only if the person or coach asks. (COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07; COACH-ANSWER PER-05; counting PROPOSED)

R8 Maintenance phase: length chosen and extendable; at its end the plan asks 'keep maintaining / change your plan / start a training block'. Dose 50-70 % of the last block's final 4 weeks (not floored), RIR 2-3, no intensifiers. (COACH-R2 R2-PER-06; COACH-ANSWER PER-01; factor split PROPOSED)

R9 Next block after a completed one: start x1.05, cap +1 set (max 25, priority 30), customizable; advanced lifters at the ceiling climb by load, intensifiers and a rotating priority muscle; after a cancelled block the same start. (COACH-R2 R2-VOL-06, R2-PER-05)

R10 Exercises stay fixed inside 4-6-week exercise blocks; between them 1-2 one-detail variations of library exercises, never invented ones; A/B lead-lift weeks only for variety seekers; heavy squat and heavy deadlift on two different days. (COACH-ANSWER PER-02, PER-03; COACH-R2 R2-LIB-01, R2-SES-01, R2-SES-02)

R11 Tests: before the block (or in week 1) and in the last week, never during the block; anyone without a completed block tests submaximally (5RM/3RM, 80-90 % efforts), never a 1RM or a max-effort mile from zero; reminders at block start, 7 days and 1 day before. (COACH-R2 R2-PER-07)

R12 Yearly plan (gen-pop 'stay in shape'): Q1 hard work + more cardio, start cutting, sets at the starting level; Q2 summer shape; Q3 maintain at ~70 %; Q4 build muscle, less cardio; last 2 weeks of December automatic maintenance; user's hemisphere and own holiday weeks; fully tunable. Athletes follow their season. (COACH-R2 R2-PER-01, R2-PER-02)

R13 Competitive athletes: season start date + practice/game days -> off-season (stairway blocks, VOL 1 -> 2 -> 3), pre-season (4-6 weeks at ~60 % with speed/power and a 1-2-week taper), in-season (2 gym days, low volume; game-heavy sports: plyos ~half, no extra COD, sprints only for speed athletes, hard day >= 48 h before a game), post-season recovery. (COACH-ANSWER PER-08, PER-11; COACH-R2 R2-GEN-05, R2-PER-06, R2-ATH-07)

R14 Athletic work has its own budget; Receive-Create stages RC1 Land -> RC2 Land & Go -> RC3 Repeat (12-week 1-3 / 4-7 / 8-12; 8-week 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-8; restart each off-season; hold in maintenance); end-of-block plyo shares by sport, each block starting 15 points more ballistic. (COACH-ANSWER VOL-10, CAT-10; COACH-R2 R2-ATH-01, R2-ATH-03)

R15 Olympic lifts for everyone in athletic training, up to 4 days a week (clean days = squat pattern, snatch days = hinge pattern); weight by RIR/RPE and speed unless a tested max; full lifts 3-5 reps per set; in-season a light 2 x 3, dropped in heavy game weeks; 60+ none by default (option with a warning); youth from the floor from ~14 after a hang block. (COACH-ANSWER ATH-10; COACH-R2 R2-ATH-04, R2-ATH-05, R2-ATH-08, R2-GEN-06)

R16 Effort stays inside 1-3 RIR: 3 RIR in the first half (the '2'), 2 RIR after halfway, 1-2 RIR in the last weeks and 1 RIR plus intensifiers (MYO, supersets; MAX only on small-muscle or bodyweight work) in the final week (the '11'); never to failure on heavy compounds. (COACH-ANSWER VOL-13, GEN-08; COACH-R2 R2-PER-05; drift PROPOSED as in 12_volume_algorithm v1.1 §3.7.2)

R17 Stay athletic and active (gen pop: pickleball, HYROX and other recreational activities): the weekend-warrior athletic overlay inside the gen-pop stairway or year; play days count like practice/game days; an optional event date ends the last block with a 1-week taper. (COACH-R2 REQ; COACH-ANSWER ATH-13; rules PROPOSED)

rules.value: +4-6 sets on the start, cap about 25-30 (optional 'pro' level above 30 for very advanced people who insist), 1-2 muscles at a time; the other muscles grow at most 3 % a week while a priority runs; the priority exercise goes first in its session

planned_step_pct.lambda: if start x growth > cap, every step of that muscle is multiplied by one factor λ < 1 so the planned peak lands on the cap in week N (12-week big muscles: L1 0.76, L2 0.87, L3 0.50; 8-week: L1 1, L2 1, L3 0.78)

value.halves: first half = weeks 2..ceil(N/2); second half = weeks ceil(N/2)+1..N (week 1 has no step). 12 weeks: 3 % in weeks 2-6, 5 % in weeks 7-12; 8 weeks: 3 % in weeks 2-4, 5 % in weeks 5-8.
value.checkin: planned + 2 points if too easy (max 7 %); hold on 9; any 10 ('the max I could do, but successful') = hold and -1 set on that day; optional 'failed' = hold, that exercise -1 set and a lighter load or easier variant (PROPOSED); under half the sessions = repeat the week; pain = pain protocol (12 v1.1 §3.7.3; R2-VOL-01 without its life column, R2-VOL-02, R2-GEN-04)

Every L1 muscle starts at 10 (12 v1.1) and would release together, pushing the total to +10.0 % (week 6 of 12, week 5 of 8), so the smallest banks wait one week (staggering PROPOSED).

deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.rule: Recovery (deload) week = about HALF the sets of the hardest (last) week (round up, min 1 per exercise), the same exercises, lighter load or 3+ RIR, no buy-outs, finishers, MYO or supersets. Athletic work: landings / low amplitude at about half the contacts and throws; conditioning easy (Orange) only.

deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.v1: Deload = about HALF the sets of the current week (round up, minimum 1 per exercise), the same exercises, lighter load or 3+ RIR, no buy-outs, finishers, MYO or supersets. Athletic work: landings / low amplitude at about half the contacts and throws; conditioning easy (Orange) only.

deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.rule: 12-week block: NO deload or maintenance week inside. One recovery week sits after week 12 and before the next block's week 1 (the approved 'week 1 of the next cycle is a deload', counted as an extra week so the next block keeps its 12 stairway weeks). No recovery week when a maintenance phase follows or precedes.
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.status: COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07 ('It should never be thrown in the middle of a block'); counting PROPOSED (14.3 #2)
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.v1: 12-week cycle: no deload at a fixed week. A deload happens when the logs trigger it (D6), and the first week of the NEXT cycle is a deload (skip it when a maintenance block came between).

deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.rule: 8-week block: same as D2 (nothing inside; one recovery week after week 8 when another block follows).
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.v1: 8-week plan: no planned deload inside (it 'starts hard' and drives weeks 5-8); triggered deloads only; the next plan opens with a deload or a maintenance block.

deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.rule: Maintenance phase for: a cancelled block; the end of a block when the person or coach asks; vacation, travel, moving; user-marked holiday weeks; the automatic last 2 weeks of December; year Q3; the athlete's season change (pre-season, D8). The user picks its length (default 4 weeks) and can add weeks; at its end the plan stops and asks 'Keep maintaining / Change your plan / Start a training block' (no answer -> keep maintaining, PROPOSED). Volume 50-70 % of the last block's final 4 weeks (50 % vacation/limited equipment, 60 % travel/moving/season change, 70 % planned maintenance and year Q3; older adults >= 70 %), not floored (the floor of 10 is for training blocks); flat; RIR 2-3; no intensifiers; loads kept, sets cut. Afterwards a whole new block from week 1.
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-01 (50-70 %, uses); COACH-R2 R2-PER-06 (length chosen, extendable, prompt), R2-VOL-07 (cancel flow), R2-PER-01 (Q3 ~70 %); factor split, older floor and default answer PROPOSED; floor reading as 12_volume_algorithm v1.1 §3.3
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.v1: A 4-6-week maintenance/transition block replaces loading when life needs it: vacation (1-2 weeks inside it), travel, moving, season change (off -> in), or planned maintenance. Volume about 50-70 % of the last block (50 % vacation/limited equipment, 60 % travel/moving/season change, 70 % planned maintenance; older adults >= 70 %), rate 0, RIR 2-3, no intensifiers; keep the loads, cut the sets.

deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.rule: Vacation and holiday weeks are maintenance weeks (50 % with what is available, or full rest). Planned ahead: the planner places them between blocks. Marked after a block has started and inside it: that block ends early (D6 flow) unless the user removes the mark. Return: a new block at the previous start.
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-01; COACH-R2 R2-PER-02, R2-VOL-07; placement PROPOSED (14.3 #1); SCIENCE Hwang 2017, Bosquet 2013
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.v1: Vacation of 1-2 weeks: train at ~50 % with what is available (bodyweight, hotel gym), or rest completely; return at the previous start (no opening deload, no level step).

deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.rule: No triggered deload (the v1 D6 is retired). The plan shows a block-at-risk prompt ('continue the block' or 'cancel it and start a maintenance phase'; it never inserts lighter weeks by itself) when, with check-ins: 2 hold weeks in a row; effort mostly 9-10 two weeks in a row; under half the sessions 2 weeks running; 'Felt a PAIN' on 2+ exercises in one week; or the person taps 'I can't keep up'. The person or coach decides: continue (holds and repeated weeks are allowed) or cancel -> maintenance phase (D4) -> a whole new block from week 1 at the same start. Without check-ins there are no signals and the block runs as planned.
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.status: COACH-R2 R2-VOL-07 ('If they can't complete it, they should cancel the block and start a maintenance phase'), R2-VOL-03; offer signals PROPOSED
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.v1: Early (unplanned) deload when: 2 weeks of hold in a row; median EFFORT >= 9 two weeks in a row; 'Felt a PAIN' on 2+ slots in one week; or performance down on 3+ main lifts for 2 exposures. After it, resume at the volume of 2 weeks before.

deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.rule: Tests are ticked at the start of the block (or 'No need for testing'). Baseline before the block or in week 1 (week 1 is the light '2' week); end test in the last week, replacing that week's top sets; the rest of that week at about 50-70 % of its sets. Never during the block. Anyone who has not completed a training block (new, untrained, or back after 6+ months off) tests submaximally: 5RM or 3RM for strength, 80-90 % efforts for cardio and speed; never a 1RM or a max-effort mile from zero. The previous block's end test is the next block's baseline.
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-07; COACH-R2 R2-PER-07 (before + end only; submax from zero; menu and reminders approved); rest-of-week dose and baseline reuse PROPOSED; SCIENCE Reynolds 2006, Pritchard 2016
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.v1: Tests are chosen by checkbox at the start of the block, or 'No need for testing'. The test day sits in the last week of the block and replaces that week's top sets; the rest of that week runs at about 50-70 % of its sets. Reminders before the test (section 6.1).

deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.rule: Taper = the last 1-2 weeks before a season opener, event or fight: volume about -40-60 % (progressive), intensity and frequency kept, no new exercises. Athletes: inside the 4-6-week pre-season block (1 week for a 4-5-week pre-season, 2 weeks for 6). Swimmers' main championship meet: 2 weeks of dryland taper lined up with the pool taper (PROPOSED, 14.3 #6). Gen-pop events (HYROX race, tournament, 10K): 1 week.
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.status: COACH-R2 R2-PER-06 ('ending with a 1-2-week taper before the first game'); COACH-ANSWER PER-08; SCIENCE Bosquet 2007, Pritchard 2016, Vachon 2020, Aouani 2024; swim and gen-pop lengths PROPOSED
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.v1: Before a season opener, event or fight: 1-2 weeks, volume -40-60 % (progressive), intensity and frequency kept, no new exercises.

deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.rule: Post-season / end of a throwing block: a recovery week that is not a scaled copy (arm care, mobility, easy aerobic, no main lifts), then general work or a maintenance phase before the next off-season.
deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.v1: Post-season / end of a throwing block: a recovery week that is not a scaled copy (arm care, mobility, easy aerobic, no main lifts), then general work before the next off-season.

deload_test_taper_rules_v1_1.v1: Yearly mode: the last 2 weeks of December switch automatically to maintenance (about 50-70 %; default 60 %), any equipment, RIR 2-3; January restarts at the previous start.

block_flow_v1_1.diagram:
TRAINING BLOCK (a stairway: week 1 feels like a '2' ... last week feels like an '11')
  baseline test before the block or in week 1 (if ticked; submax if no completed block)
  weeks run in order; holds, repeated weeks and pain swaps are allowed; NO deload or maintenance week inside
  |
  +-- block COMPLETED -> end test in the last week (if ticked) -> END-OF-BLOCK CHOICE (PROPOSED):
  |      (a) next block (default for week-by-week, year and repeat plans):
  |          RECOVERY WEEK (about half the sets of the hardest week, same exercises, 3+ RIR)
  |          -> next block week 1 at start x1.05, cap +1
  |      (b) maintenance phase (the person or coach asks; choose its length) -> see below
  |      (c) change the plan (new goal or program)
  |
  +-- block CANNOT be completed -> the person or coach taps CANCEL (the plan only offers it)
         -> MAINTENANCE PHASE (choose the number of weeks; add weeks any time)
         -> END-OF-MAINTENANCE PROMPT: 'Keep maintaining' | 'Change your plan' | 'Start a training block'
         -> a whole new block from week 1 at the SAME start as the cancelled block (no recovery week: maintenance was the recovery)
end_of_block_choice: Next block one step up (recovery week first)

science_grounding_v1_1.his_rule: 'The first 2 to 4 weeks are going to be just you getting used to the movements' (PER-01)
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Damas 2016: hypertrophy signal mostly after ~3 weeks, once damage drops; repeated bout effect: early exposures protect
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Supported. v1.1: these are the first small steps of the stairway (3 %, λ-scaled) at 3 RIR.

science_grounding_v1_1.shape: 12-week stairway: small steps to halfway, bigger after, last 4 weeks hardest
science_grounding_v1_1.his_rule: 'steps up a stairway ... that goes for every plan' (R2-PER-03); 'the last 4 weeks are going to be brutal' (R2-PER-04)
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: RP/Enes/Pelland: more weekly sets -> more growth with diminishing returns; Grgic 2017, Harries 2015, Moesgaard 2022: the periodization model matters little when volume is equal; Williams 2017: planned plans beat unplanned for strength
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Supported: a gradual volume ramp to a hard finish, then recovery, is the RP mesocycle logic; equal-volume models give similar growth (Grgic 2017), so the value is in the gradual ramp and the planned recovery.

science_grounding_v1_1.shape: No deload inside a block; a recovery week between blocks
science_grounding_v1_1.his_rule: 'It should never be thrown in the middle of a block' (R2-VOL-07)
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Rogerson 2024: deload every ~5.6 weeks in practice; Bell 2023: planned or autoregulated both acceptable; Coleman 2024: a 1-week break mid-program did not change growth
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Plausible: Coleman 2024 found a mid-program week off did not help growth; practitioners deload every ~5-6 weeks (Rogerson 2024), so his blocks rely on the 2 -> 11 stair, holds and the cancel option; the recovery week between blocks matches the Bell 2023 placement option.

science_grounding_v1_1.his_rule: R2-PER-03 (NOT RIGHT on 4 + 4 and 'start hard'): the same stairway as every plan
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Scarpelli 2022 / Barsuhn 2024 (in 12_vol): trained people do well starting from their previous volume; repeated bout effect
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Supported: the same gradual ramp; the repeated bout effect and Damas 2016 favour small early steps.

science_grounding_v1_1.his_rule: 'a lower-volume maintenance volume ... 70 % ... 50 %. This allows them to recover and not push too hard' (PER-01)
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Bickel 2011 (1/3 of the dose keeps size in the young), Spiering 2021, Bosquet 2013 (strength stable ~4 weeks off), Ogasawara 2013 (breaks do not cost long-term growth)
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Well supported; older adults stay >= 70 %; even a beginner's 6-9 sets are above the research minimum for keeping size (Bickel 2011).

science_grounding_v1_1.his_rule: 'start at a 2 and end at an 11' (PER-01)
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Scarpelli 2022 (progressing from the person's own previous volume worked); Pelland 2026 (each extra step of growth costs more sets); Ogasawara 2013
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Supported with a ceiling: advanced clients climb by load, intensifiers and a rotating priority muscle, not only sets (approved, COACH-R2 R2-PER-05).

science_grounding_v1_1.his_rule: 'Just keep me in line ... and then it does it by itself' (PER-01)
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Kiely 2012 (responsive planning), Hickmott 2022 (autoregulation as good as % plans; in 12_vol)
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Supported: rolling stairways with the optional check-in (Kiely 2012; Hickmott 2022 in 12_vol).

science_grounding_v1_1.his_rule: R2-PER-01/02 (approved for gen-pop 'stay in shape'; user-tunable)
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: No controlled trials of annual plans for general clients (Afonso 2017: no periodization trial longer than ~9 months); Issurin/Kiely frameworks; Murphy & Koehler 2022 (cut phases protect muscle, not grow it); Yanovski 2000 / Diaz-Zavala 2017 (holiday gain)
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Coaching choice with sensible support; approved by the coach for gen pop.

science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Bompa step/wave loading (practitioner); taper evidence (Bosquet 2007, Pritchard 2016); no hypertrophy advantage for any model (Grgic 2017)
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Supported as a peaking tool; smooth stays the default elsewhere.

science_grounding_v1_1.shape: Returning after a layoff (6-12+ months off) and ex-pros
science_grounding_v1_1.his_rule: body treated as a beginner, skills come back fast; ex-pros at Level 1 only briefly (PRG-05)
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Psilander 2019, Blocquiaux 2020: strength and skill persist longer than size; regaining takes about half the time off
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Supported: L1 volume with a 4-week acclimation, exercise level kept, level-up check after the first block (PROPOSED).

science_grounding_v1_1.his_rule: 'a vacation 1-week or vacation 2-week kind of thing' (PER-01)
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Hwang 2017: strength and lean mass kept after 2 weeks off; Bosquet 2013: maximal strength mostly kept up to ~4 weeks
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Supported: ~50 % with what is available, or full rest; return at the previous start.

science_grounding_v1_1.shape: Strength %-template and Olympic ramp (PER-09: 'I just want to make sure it's correct')
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: RTS RPE chart (section 5.3); NSCA power guidance (75-85 % for 3-5 reps); Suchomel 2017 (pull variants allow heavier loads); Harries 2015 (linear steps as good as undulating for strength)
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Main lift: consistent (loads within about 1-4 points of the chart). Olympic 4 x 8 @ 75 %: high for full catch lifts; fine for DB/KB and pull variants; flagged (14.2). v1.1: full squat cleans/snatches use 3-5 reps per set (R2-ATH-05); weight by RPE and speed unless a tested max (R2-GEN-06).

science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Issurin 2010: accumulation 2-6 weeks -> transmutation 2-4 -> realization; strength residuals ~30 +/- 5 days, explosive ~5 +/- 3 days; Painter 2012
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Supported; keep plyos/sprints in every phase because explosive residuals are short.

science_grounding_v1_1.shape: Testing before and after, submax from zero
science_grounding_v1_1.his_rule: R2-PER-07: test before and at the end, never mid-block; 5RM/3RM or 80-90 % from zero
science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Reynolds 2006: a 5RM predicted the 1RM best (R2 0.99 bench, 0.97 leg press) in adults of mixed experience aged 18-69
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Supported: safe baselines lose little accuracy.

science_grounding_v1_1.evidence: Bosquet 2007 (taper 8-14 days, volume -41-60 %, intensity kept); Vachon 2020 (team sports); Ronnestad 2011 / Spiering 2021 (maintenance with low volume when intensity is kept)
Bosquet 2007; Aouani 2024 (2-week progressive taper, +3.5 % 50 m time)
science_grounding_v1_1.verdict: Supported: 2-week dryland taper lined up with the pool taper (PROPOSED).

season_calendar_v1_1.inputs: next season start date (first game) or 'in season until', plus practice days and game days per week (R2-GEN-05)
rule: In season now -> IN-SEASON until the 'in season until' date -> POST-SEASON 1-2 weeks -> OFF-SEASON.
W = weeks from the plan start to the first game. PRE-SEASON = the last 6 weeks (4 when W is 7-9), ending with the taper (1 week for 4-5 weeks, 2 for 6); W <= 6 -> pre-season only (W weeks).

OFF-SEASON = the weeks before the pre-season: 12-week block if >= 12 weeks remain (earlier weeks: a 4-8-week foundation block, or general/maintenance weeks if fewer than 4; L1-L2 athletes with >= 16 weeks may run STARTING -> MID -> ADVANCED as blocks, PRG-04 PROPOSED); 8-week block if 8-11 remain; a short 4-7-week stairway if 4-7 remain; 1-3 leftover weeks run as general weeks.
Off-season blocks are stairways with a recovery week between them; the pre-season starts right after the last off-season block (its lower volume is the unload).
season_calendar_v1_1.engine_thresholds: close to the engine's D-15 thresholds (>= 20 weeks OFF_EARLY, >= 12 OFF_BUILD, >= 6 OFF_LATE, else PRE), which put the pre-season boundary one week later than this 6-week pre-season: D-15 should read PRE when 6 weeks or fewer remain (integrator)

rules.rule: a race or tournament date turns the last block into a peak: its hardest weeks end 1 week before the event, then a 1-week taper (about half the sets, intensity kept). No date -> the normal stairway or year.

the approved gen-pop year stays the default; the user can drop an athletic block where they want it (e.g. a pickleball-season block in spring, a HYROX block before a race) by re-ordering or changing blocks.

retired_v1_1.autoregulation_note_v1_1: v1.1: the plan works without tracking; the optional 1-minute weekly check-in (effort, completion, how it felt, pain; no life question) moves the step (R2-GEN-01, R2-GEN-04); no check-in = planned stairway (R2-VOL-03); no deload inside a block (R2-VOL-07)
retired_v1_1.generator_pseudocode_v1_1:
generate_plan(client):                                   # v1.1 (round-2 answers applied)
  level  = level_from_experience(years, months_off, ex_pro)   # L1/L2/L3 (PRG-05)
  family = map_goal(goal)       # HYPERTROPHY | STRENGTH | FAT_LOSS | GENERAL (incl. 'stay athletic & active') | HYBRID | ATHLETE
  mode   = client.plan_mode     # C12 | C8 | MAINT(weeks chosen) | WBW | YEAR ; overlays PREP(date) | SEASON(season start, practice/game days)
  tests  = client.test_ticks    # strength / cardio / speed / jumps / body, or 'No need for testing' (R2-PER-07)
  # NO lifestyle inputs (R2-GEN-04): nothing below reads sleep, stress or job

  if SEASON: phases = season_calendar(start_date, season_start, practice_days, game_days)   # R2-GEN-05, R2-PER-06 (8.2.0)
  grid    = STAIRWAY_GRID[mode](level, q1_cut)   # q1_cut: year Q1 holds sets at the level start (R2-PER-01); week -> phase (ACCLIMATION/DRIVE/HARDEST), planned step, stair level 2..11, RIR, exercise block, RC stage
  overlay = FAMILY_OVERLAY[family]              # phase -> reps, effort, load, methods, laterality, conditioning, athletic content
  start   = volume_engine.start(level, family, season, priorities, pain)   # 12_volume_algorithm v1.1
  if previous_block == COMPLETED: start *= 1.05; cap += 1   (cap <= 25, priority 30)          # R2-VOL-06
  if previous_block == CANCELLED: start = previous_start                                  # R2-VOL-07
  if previous_block == COMPLETED and not maintenance_between: emit(RECOVERY_WEEK(half_sets(previous_last_week)))  # R2-VOL-07

  if tests: schedule baseline before the block or in week 1 (submax if no completed block)  # R2-PER-07
  for week in grid:                                        # never a deload or maintenance week inside (R2-VOL-07)
      step = week.planned_step                              # stairway 3 % -> 5 %, x lambda so the peak lands on the cap (R2-PER-03/04; 12 v1.1); 60+ <= 3 %
      if checkin(week-1) exists: step = read_against_stairway(step, effort, completion, pain)   # +2 pts if too easy (max 7 %), hold on 9/10, -1 set on that day after a 10, 'failed' = hold + lighter (R2-VOL-01 minus life, R2-VOL-02, R2-GEN-04)
      # no check-in -> planned step unchanged (R2-VOL-03)
      if under_half_sessions: repeat_week (or hold if a fixed date is ahead)     # R2-VOL-01
      T = min(cap, T * (1 + step)); place whole sets while T - current >= 1, total rise < 10 %   # VOL-06, VOL-07, UNI-05 (12 v1.1)
      if no set released: raise load/reps or step the RIR target                   # every week climbs (R2-PER-05)
      apply overlay[week.phase] -> reps, RIR, methods (MYO last isolation; supersets as a fatigue tool; contrast off-season int+)
      athletic block (own budget): plyo share start = end - 15 -> end (R2-ATH-01); RC stage by week (R2-ATH-03);
          Olympic up to 4 days, clean days = squat pattern, snatch days = hinge pattern, by RPE/speed unless a tested max (R2-ATH-04/05, R2-GEN-06);
          60+: Olympic lifts, plyos (ankle hops included) and depth jumps off by default, opt-in with the warning (R2-ATH-08)
      if season phase == IN: 2 days; game-heavy rule (R2-ATH-07); Olympic 2 x 3, none in heavy game weeks (R2-ATH-04)
      if week.exercise_block_boundary: one-detail changes (R2-LIB-01); level-up eligible slots (PER-06)
      if week.is_last and tests: end test replaces the top sets; reminders at start, -7 d, -1 d   # R2-PER-07
      if block_at_risk(checkins): ASK continue | cancel -> maintenance(weeks chosen) -> prompt -> new block   # R2-VOL-07, R2-PER-06
  after the block: END-OF-BLOCK CHOICE (next block | maintenance | change plan)                 # PROPOSED

open_questions_v1_1.question: A holiday or vacation week marked INSIDE a block that has already started: do we end the block there (your 'cancel -> maintenance -> new block' rule), or let that one week be a lighter 'hold' week and continue the block?
open_questions_v1_1.proposal: The year planner always puts marked weeks between blocks. A week marked after a block started ends that block early (the user is warned and can remove the mark).

open_questions_v1_1.question: After a finished 12-week block, the half-sets recovery week: is it an extra 13th week (the next block keeps all 12 weeks), or is it week 1 of the next 12?
open_questions_v1_1.proposal: An extra week, so every block keeps its full stairway and a year quarter is 12 + 1 = 13 weeks.

open_questions_v1_1.question: Check-ins in the first half of a block: your table gives +5 % for an on-target week and +7 % for an easy week, but the stairway wants small steps early. OK that the check-in reads against the stairway?
open_questions_v1_1.proposal: On target = the planned step; too easy = the planned step + 2 points (max 7 %). First half: +3 % / +5 %; from the halfway point exactly your table (+5 % / +7 %).

open_questions_v1_1.question: 'Nobody needs less than 10 sets': does that floor also hold in maintenance phases? At 50-70 % a beginner maintains at 6-9 sets.
open_questions_v1_1.proposal: No: the floor is for training blocks; maintenance phases, pre-season and in-season keep your lower maintenance volume (50-70 %, round 1).

open_questions_v1_1.question: Events for the general population (a HYROX race, a pickleball tournament, a 10K): should the user be able to set an event date?
open_questions_v1_1.proposal: Yes: the last block ends at the event; its hardest weeks finish 1 week before, then a 1-week taper (about half the sets, same intensity). Without a date the plan runs the normal gen-pop stairway or year.

open_questions_v1_1.question: Swimmers: should the gym (dryland) taper follow the swim coach's pool taper before the main championship meet, and how long should it be? Swim research favours about 2 weeks (8-14 days, volume -41-60 %, intensity kept).
open_questions_v1_1.proposal: 2 weeks of dryland taper before the main championship meet, lined up with the pool taper; 1 week or none before smaller meets.
